chapters: And there was one man from Ramatayim Tzofim, from Mt. Efraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Yerocham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tochu, the son of Tzuf, an Efraimi.
And he had two wives; the name of the one was Chanah and the name of the second was Peninah; and Peninah had children, but Chanah had no children.

And that man was wont to go up from his city from appointed time to appointed time, to prostrate himself and to slaughter to Havayah of Hosts in Shilo, and there the two sons of Eli, Chofni and Pinchas, were serving Havayah.
And when it was the day, and Elkanah slaughtered, and he would give to Peninah his wife and to all her sons and daughters portions.
And to Chanah he would give one choice portion, for he loved Chanah, and Havayah had shut up her womb.
And her rival would frequently anger her, in order to make her complain, for Havayah had shut up her womb.
And so he would do year by year, as often as she went up to the house of Havayah, so she would anger her, and she wept and would not eat.
And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Chanah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
And Chanah arose after eating and after drinking, and Eli the priest was sitting on the chair beside the doorpost of the Temple of Havayah.
And she was bitter in spirit, and she prayed to Havayah, and wept.

And she vowed a vow, and said: to Havayah of Hosts, if You will look upon the affliction of Your bondswoman, and You will remember me, and You will not forget Your bondswoman and You will give Your bondswoman a man-child, and I shall give him to Havayah all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head.
And it was, as she prayed long before Havayah, that Eli watched her mouth.
But Chanah, she was speaking in her heart, only her lips were moving, and her voice was not heard, and Eli thought her to be a drunken woman.
And Eli said to her: Until when will you be drunk? Throw off your wine from upon yourself.
And Chanah answered and said: No, my master, I am a woman of sorrowful spirit, and neither new wine nor old wine have I drunk, and I poured out my soul before Havayah.
Deliver not your bondswoman before the unscrupulous woman, for out of the abundance of my complaint and my vexation have I spoken until now.
And Eli answered and said: Go in peace, and Elokim of Yisroel will grant your request which you have asked of Him.
And she said: May your bondswoman find favor in your eyes; and the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was not anymore.
And they arose early in the morning, and prostrated themselves before Havayah: and they returned and came to their house, to Ramah, and Elkanah knew Chanah, his wife, and Havayah remembered her.
And it was, when the time came about, after Chanah had conceived, that she bore a son, and she called his name Shmuel, because; "I asked him of Havayah."
And the man, Elkanah and his entire household, went up to slaughter to Havayah, the sacrifice of the days and his vow.
But Chanah did not go up, for she said to her husband: "Until the child is weaned, then I shall bring him, and he shall appear before Havayah, and abide there forever.
And Elkanah her husband said to her: "Do what seems good to you. Stay until you have weaned him, only, may Havayah fulfill His word." And the woman stayed and nursed her son, until she weaned him.

And she brought him with her when she had weaned him, with three bulls, and one ephah of meal, and an earthenware jug of wine, and she brought him to the house of Havayah, to Shilo, and the child was young.
And they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the child to Eli.
And she said, "Please, my master! As surely as your soul lives, my master, I am the woman who was standing here with you, to pray to Havayah.
For this child did I pray, and Havayah granted me my request, which I asked of Him.
And I also have lent him to Havayah; all the days which he will be alive, he is borrowed by Havayah." And he prostrated himself there to Havayah.
And Chanah prayed and said: "My heart has rejoiced through Havayah; My horn has been raised by Havayah. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, For I have rejoiced in Your salvation.
There is none as holy as Havayah, For there is none besides You; And there is no rock like our Elokim.
Do not increasingly speak haughtily; Let not arrogance come out of your mouth, For Havayah is an Elokim of thoughts, And to Him are deeds counted.
The bows of the mighty are broken; And those who stumbled, are girded with strength.
Those who were satiated have hired themselves out for bread, While the hungry have ceased. While the barren woman has born seven, She that had many children, has been bereaved.
Havayah kills and makes alive; He brings down to the grave and raises up.
Havayah impoverishes and makes rich. He humbles; He also exalts.

He lifts the poor from the dust; From the dunghill, He raises the pauper, To seat them with princes, And a seat of honor He causes them to inherit, For the pillars of the earth are Havayah's, And He placed the world upon them.
The feet of His pious ones He will guard, And the wicked shall be cut off in darkness, For not by strength will man prevail.

Those who strive with Havayah will be broken; Upon him will He thunder in Heaven; Havayah will judge the ends of the earth. And He will grant strength to His king, And raise the horn of His anointed one.
And Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house, and the child was serving Havayah before Eli the priest.
And Eli's sons, unscrupulous men, knew not Havayah.
And this was the due of the priests from the people: any man would slaughter a sacrifice, the servant of the priest would come when cooked the flesh, with a three-pronged fork in his hand.

And he would thrust into the fire-pot, or into the pot, or into the cauldron, or into the pan, everything which the fork would pick up, the priest would take therewith; so would they do to all Yisroel who came there in Shilo.

Also, before they would make the fat smoke, and the servant of the priest would come, and would say to the man who slaughtered, 'Give meat to roast for the priest, and he will not take from you cooked meat, but raw.
And the man said to him, 'Let them make the fat smoke now, and take for yourself, as your soul desires,' And he would say, 'No, but now you shall give. And if not, I shall take by force.'
And the sin of the lads was great before Havayah, for the men despised the offering of Havayah.
And Shmuel was serving before Havayah, being a lad girded with a linen robe.
And a small robe his mother would make for him, and she would bring it up to him from appointed time to appointed time, when she ascended with her husband, to slaughter the sacrifice of the days.
And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, and he would say, "May Havayah grant you seed from this woman," because of the request which he had requested of Havayah, and they would go to his place.
For Havayah remembered Chanah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the lad Shmuel grew up with Havayah.
Now, Eli had become very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Yisroel, and that they would lie with the women who congregated at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And he said to them: "Why do you do the likes of these things, for I hear evil reports about you, from all these people.
No, my sons, for the rumor which I hear Havayah's people spreading, is not good.

If man will sin to man, the judge will judge him. If, however, he will sin against Elokim, who will intercede in the judgment in his behalf?" But they would not hearken to their father's voice, for Havayah desired to kill them.
And the lad, Shmuel, was growing up, and bettering himself both with Havayah and with people.
And a man of Elokim came to Eli, and he said to him: "So Havayah said: 'Did I appear to the house of your father, when they were in Mitzrayim, to the house of Paroh?

And did I choose him from all the tribes of Yisroel to be My priest, to offer up on My altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before Me? And did I give to the house of your father all the fire-offerings of the children of Yisroel?

Why do you kick at My sacrifice, and at My meal offering which I commanded in My dwelling place, and you honored your sons above Me, before My people, to feed yourselves from the first part of every offering of Yisroel?

Therefore," Havayah says, Elokim of Yisroel, "I said, 'Your house and the house of your father will walk before Me forever,' but now, Havayah says: Far be it from Me, for those who honor Me shall I honor, and those who despise Me will be disgraced.
Behold days are coming when I shall cut off your arm and the arm of your father's house, that there shall not be an elder in your household.
And you will look upon a rival dwelling place in all which will do good to Yisroel, and there will not be an elder in your household all of the days.
Yet every man of yours shall I not cut off from My altar, to disappoint you and to sadden your heart; and all those raised in your house will die as young men.
And this is the sign to you, that which will befall your two sons, Chofni and Pinchas; in one day both of them will die.
And I shall raise up for Myself a faithful priest, who will do as is in My heart and in My mind, and I shall build for him a sure house, and he shall walk before My anointed all of the days.

And it will be that everyone who is left in your house, will come to prostrate himself before him for a silver piece and a morsel of bread, and will say, "Take me now into one of the priestly divisions in order to eat a morsel of bread."
And the lad Shmuel was serving Havayah before Eli. Now the word of Havayah was withheld in those days; vision had not broken through.
And it was on that day, that Eli was lying in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow dim; he could not see.
And the lamp of Elokim had not yet gone out, and Shmuel was lying down. In the Temple of Havayah, where the Ark of Elokim was.
Havayah called Shmuel, and he said, "Here I am."
And he ran to Eli, and said, "Here I am, for you have called me." And he said, "I did not call. Go back and lie down." And he went and lay down.
And Havayah continued to call again to Shmuel, and Shmuel arose, and went to Eli, and said, "Here I am, for you have called me.'' And he said, "I have not called, my son. Go back and lie down."
Now, Shmuel had not yet known Havayah, and the word of Havayah had not yet been revealed to him.
And Havayah continued to call Shmuel for the third time; and he arose and went to Eli, and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And Eli understood that Havayah was calling the youth.
And Eli said to Shmuel, "Go, lie down. And it shall be, if He will call you, that you shall say, 'Speak, O Havayah, for Your bondsman is listening.' " And Shmuel went and lay down in his place.
And Havayah came and stood, and He called as at the other times, "Shmuel! Shmuel!" And Shmuel said, "Speak, for Your bondsman is listening."
And Havayah said to Shmuel, "Behold, I am about to do something in Yisroel, about which the two ears of everyone who hears it, will tingle.
On that day, I shall execute against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his household, beginning and ending.
And I have told him that I am about to execute judgment upon his household forever, for the iniquity that he knew that his sons were bringing disgrace upon themselves, and he did not rebuke them.
And, therefore, I have sworn to the house of Eli, that the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be purged by sacrifice or by offering forever."
And Shmuel lay down until the morning, and he opened the doors of the House of Havayah. And Shmuel was afraid to relate the vision to Eli.
And Eli called Shmuel, and said, "Shmuel, my son!" And he said, "Here I am."

And he said, "What is the thing which He spoke to you? Do not conceal from me now. So shall Elokim do to you, and so shall He continue, if you conceal from me anything of the whole matter which He spoke to you."
And Shmuel told him all the things and did not conceal from him. And he said, "He is Havayah. May He do what is good in His eyes."
And Shmuel grew up, and Havayah was with him, and did not let any of his words fall to the ground.
And all Yisroel from Dan to Be'er Sheva, knew that Shmuel was established as a prophet to Havayah.
And Havayah continued to appear in Shilo, for Havayah revealed Himself to Shmuel in Shilo with the word of Havayah.
And the word of Shmuel was to all Yisroel and Yisroel went out to war against the Pelishtim, and they encamped beside Ebenezer, and the Pelishtim encamped in Afek.
And the Pelishtim arrayed against Yisroel, and the battle spread, and Yisroel was beaten before the Pelishtim, and they slew in the battle array in the field, about four thousand men.

And the people came to the camp, and the elders of Yisroel said, "Why has Havayah beaten us today before the Pelishtim? Let us take to us from Shilo the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah, and He will come in our midst, and save us from the hand of our enemies."

And the people sent to Shilo, and from there, they carried the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah of Hosts, Who dwells above the cherubim, and there with the Ark of Elokim's Covenant, were Eli's two sons, Chofni and Pinchas.
And it was, when the Ark of Havayah's Covenant came into the camp, that all Yisroel shouted a great shout, and the earth stirred.
And the Pelishtim heard the sound of the shout, and they said, "What is the sound of this great shout in the camp of the Ivrim?" And they knew that the Ark of Havayah had come into the camp.
And the Pelishtim feared, for they said, "Elokim has come into the camp." And they said, "Woe is unto us, for there was nothing like this yesterday and before yesterday!"
"Woe is unto us! Who will save us from the hand of this mighty Elokim? This is Elokim who smote the Mitzrim with every sort of plague in the wilderness."
"Strengthen yourselves and become men, you Pelishtim, lest you serve the Ivrim, as they served you, and you shall become men, and fight!"
And the Pelishtim waged war and Yisroel was beaten, and they fled, each man to his tents. Now the blow was very great, and there fell from Yisroel thirty thousand infantrymen.
And the Ark of Elokim was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Chofni and Pinchas, perished.
And a man of Binyamin ran from the battle array, and came to Shilo on that day, with his garments torn, and earth upon his head.

And he came, and behold, Eli was sitting on the chair beside the road, anxiously waiting, for his heart trembled for the Ark of Elokim. And the man had come to tell in the city, and the whole city cried out.
Now Eli heard the sound of the cry, and he said, "What is this confused noise?" And the man hurried, and came, and told Eli.
Now Eli was ninety- eight years old, and his eyes were set, and he could not see.
And the man said to Eli, "I am the one who has come from the battle array, and I fled from the battle array today." And he said, "What happened, my son?"

And the one who had reported the news, answered and said, "Yisroel fled before the Pelishtim, and also there was a great slaughter among the people, and also your two sons perished, Chofni and Pinchas and the Ark of Elokim was taken."

And it was, when he mentioned the Ark of Elokim, that he fell off the chair backward through the gate opening, and his neck broke and he died, because the man was old and weighty and he had judged Yisroel for forty years.

And his daughter-in-law, Pinchas' wife, was with child, ready to give birth, and she heard the news concerning the taking of the Ark of Elokim, and that her father-in-law and her husband had died. And she knelt and gave birth, for her pains had suddenly come upon her.
And about the time of her dying, the women who were standing by her, said, "Do not fear, for you have borne a son," and she did not answer, neither did she heed.
And she called the child I-Kavod, saying, "Glory has been exiled from Yisroel, because the Ark of Elokim has been taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband."
And she said, "Glory has been exiled from Yisroel, for the Ark of Elokim has been taken."
Now, the Pelishtim had taken the Ark of Elokim, and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
And the Pelishtim took the Ark of Elokim and brought it to the house of Dagon, and set it up beside Dagon.
And the Ashdodim arose early on the morrow, and behold, Dagon was falling face downward to the ground before the Ark of Havayah, and they returned him to his place.

And they arose early the next morning, and behold, Dagon was falling face downward to the ground, before the Ark of Havayah, and Dagon's head and the two palms of his hands were cut off, on the threshold; only Dagon alone remained upon him.
Therefore, the priests of Dagon and all those who come to the house of Dagon, do not tread upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod until this day.
And the hand of Havayah became heavy upon the Ashdodim, and He ravaged them, and He smote them with hemorrhoids, Ashdod and its borders.
And the people of Ashdod saw that it was so, and they said, "Let not the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel dwell with us, for His hand is severe upon us and upon Dagon, our deity.

And they sent and gathered all the lords of the Pelishtim unto them, and they said, "What shall we do to the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel?" And they said, "Let the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel be brought around to Gat," and, they brought the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel around to Gat.

And it was, after they had brought it around, that the hand of Havayah was upon the city a great panic, and He smote the people of the city, both young and old, and hemorrhoids broke out in their hidden parts.

And they sent away the Ark of Elokim to Ekron, and it was that when the Ark of Elokim came to Ekron, that the Ekronim cried out, saying, "They have brought around the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel to me to kill me and my people.

And they sent and gathered all the lords of the Pelishtim, and they said, "Send away the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel, and let it return to its place, so that it will not kill me and my people," for there was a panic of death in the entire city; the hand of Elokim was very heavy there.
And the people who did not die, were smitten with hemorrhoids, and the cry of the city ascended to heaven.
And the Ark of Havayah was in the field of the Pelishtim seven months.
And the Pelishtim called the priests and the diviners, saying, "What shall we do to the Ark of Havayah? Let us know in what we shall send it to its place."

And they said, "If you send the Ark of Elokim of Yisroel, do not send it away empty, but you shall send back with it a guilt-offering. Then you will be cured, and it will be known to you, why His hand would not turn away from you.

And they said, "What is the guilt-offering which we shall send back to Him?" And they said, "The number of the lords of the Pelishtim: five hemorrhoids of gold and five mice of gold, for there is one plague for all of them and for your lords.

And you shall make the images of your hemorrhoids and the images of your mice who destroy the land, and you shall give honor to Elokim of Yisroel. Perhaps He will lighten His hand from upon you, and from upon your deity, and from upon your land.
And why should you make your heart heavy as the Mitzrim and Paroh made their hearts heavy? Will it not be, just as He mocked them, and they sent them away, and they departed?
And now take and make one new cart, and two milch cows, upon which no yoke has come, and you shall hitch the cows to the cart, and return their young home from behind them.

And you shall take the Ark of Havayah, and you shall place it on the cart, and the golden objects which you have sent back to Him as a guilt-offering, you shall place in the box at its side, and you shall send it away, and it will go.

And you will see, if it goes up on the way to its own boundary, to Beit-Shemesh, He wrought upon us this great evil, and if not, then we shall know that it was not His hand which touched us; it was an accident which befell us.
And the men did so, and they took two milch cows, and hitched them to the cart, and their young they shut up in the house.
And they placed the Ark of Havayah on the cart, and the box, and the golden mice, and the images of their hemorrhoids.

And the cows went straight in the road on the way to Beit-Shemesh, on one highway, lowing as they went, and they turned neither to the right nor to the left. And the lords of the Pelishtim were going along after them as far as the border of Beit-Shemesh.
Now Beit-Shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the Ark, and they rejoiced to see.
And the cart had come to the field of Yehoshua, the Beit-Shemeshi, and stood there, and there was a huge stone. And they split the wood, and the cows, they offered up as a burnt offering to Havayah.

And the Leviim took down the Ark of Havayah, and the box which was with it, wherein were the golden objects, and they placed them on the huge stone, and the men of Beit-Shemesh offered up burnt offerings and slaughtered sacrifices on that day, to Havayah.
And the five lords of the Pelishtim had seen, and they returned to Ekron on that day.
And these were the golden hemorrhoids which the Pelishtim had sent back a guilt-offering to Havayah: one for Ashdod, one for Azah, one for Ashkelon, one for Gat, one for Ekron.

And the golden mice were according to the number of all the cities of the Pelishtim, which belonged to the five lords, from fortified city to open village and even to the great stone upon which they had placed the Ark of Havayah, until this day in the field of Yehoshua the Beit-Shemeshi.

And He smote of the people of Beit-Shemesh, for they had gazed upon the Ark of Havayah, and He smote of the people seventy men, fifty thousand men, and the people mourned, for Havayah had struck a great blow upon the people.
And the men of Beit-Shemesh said, "Who will be able to stand before Havayah, this holy Elokim? And to whom will it go up from upon us?"
And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiryat-Ye'arim, saying, "The Pelishtim have returned the Ark of Havayah. Come down, and take it up to you."
And the men of Kiryat-Ye'arim came and took up the Ark of Havayah, and brought it to the house of Avinadav, on the hill, and they designated Elazar, his son to guard the Ark of Havayah.
And it was that from the day the Ark was stationed in Kiryat-Ye'arim, that the time ran on, to twenty years, and all the house of Yisroel were drawn after Havayah.

And Shmuel said to all the house of Yisroel, saying, "If with all your heart, you are returning to Havayah, remove the foreign deities from your midst, and the Ashtarot, and direct your heart toward Havayah, and serve Him alone, and He will save you from the hand of the Pelishtim.
And the children of Yisroel removed the Be'alim and the Ashtarot, and served Havayah alone.
And Shmuel said, "Gather all Yisroel to Mitzpah, and I shall pray to Havayah on your behalf."

And they assembled at Mitzpah, and drew water, and poured before Havayah, and they fasted on that day, and said there, "We have sinned to Havayah." And Shmuel judged the children of Yisroel in Mitzpah.

Now the Pelishtim heard that the children of Yisroel had assembled at Mitzpah, and the lords of the Pelishtim went up against Yisroel, and the children of Yisroel heard, and they were afraid of the Pelishtim.
And the children of Yisroel said to Shmuel, "Cease not to cry out to Havayah our Elokim for us, that He save us from the hand of the Pelishtim."
And Shmuel took one sucking lamb and offered it up as a burnt offering, entirely to Havayah, and Shmuel cried out to Havayah on behalf of Yisroel, and Havayah answered him.

And as Shmuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Pelishtim drew near for war against Yisroel, and Havayah thundered with a loud noise on that day, upon the Pelishtim, and threw them into a panic, and they were beaten before Yisroel.
And the men of Yisroel went forth from Mitzpah, and pursued the Pelishtim, and harassed them until they were below Beit-Kar.
And Shmuel took one stone, and placed it between Mitzpah and the peak, and he called its name Ebenezer, for he said, "Hitherto Havayah has helped us."
And the Pelishtim were subdued, and they came no more into the border of Yisroel, and the hand of Havayah was upon the Pelishtim all the days of Shmuel.

And the cities which the Pelishtim had taken from Yisroel were restored to Yisroel; from Ekron to Gat, and their border, Yisroel delivered from the hand of the Pelishtim, and there was peace between Yisroel and the Emorim.
And Shmuel judged Yisroel all the days of his life.
And from year to year, he would set forth, and go around to Beit El, and Gilgal, and Mitzpah, and he would judge Yisroel in all these places.
And his return was to Ramah, for there was his house, and there he judged Yisroel, and he built there an altar to Havayah.
And it was, when Shmuel had grown old, that he appointed his sons judges for Yisroel.
And the name of his first born was Joel, and the name of the second, Aviyah; they were judges in Be'er Sheva.
And his sons did not walk in his ways, and they turned after gain, and they took bribes and perverted justice.
And all the elders of Yisroel gathered, and came to Shmuel, to Ramah.
And they said to him, "Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now, set up for us a king to judge us like all the nations."
And the thing was displeasing in the eyes of Shmuel, when they said, "Give us a king to judge us," and Shmuel prayed to Havayah.
And Havayah said to Shmuel, "Listen to the voice of the people, according to all that they will say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me from reigning over them.
Like all the deeds which they have done from the day I brought them up from Mitzrayim, and until this day, and they forsook Me and served other deities; so are they doing to you.
And now, listen to their voice; except that you shall warn them, and tell them the manner of the king who will reign over them.
And Shmuel related all the words of Havayah to the people who asked of him a king.

And he said, "This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you; he will take your sons, and appoint them to him for his chariots and for his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots.
And he will appoint them to him commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and to plow his plowing and to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons and the equipment for his chariots.
And he will take your daughters for his perfumers, for cooks, and for bakers.
And he will take the best of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive trees, and will give them to his slaves.
And he will tithe your grain crops and your vineyards, and he will give them to his officers and his slaves.
And he will take your male and female slaves, and your handsomest youths and your asses, and put them to his work.
And he will tithe your flocks, and you will be slaves to him.
And you will cry out on that day because of your king, whom you will have chosen for yourselves, and Havayah will not answer you on that day.
And the people refused to listen to Shmuel's voice, and they said, "No, but there shall be a king over us.
And also we shall be like all the nations, and our king will judge us, go forth before us and wage our wars."
And Shmuel heard all the words of the people, and he spoke to them in the ears of Havayah.
And Havayah said to Shmuel, "Listen to their voice, and you shall make them a king." And Shmuel said to the men of Yisroel, "Go, every man to his city."
Now there was a man of Binyamin, and his name was Kish, the son of Aviel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bekorat, the son of Afiach, the son of a Binyamini man, a mighty man of power.
And he had a son whose name was Shaul. He was young and handsome, there being no one of the children of Yisroel handsomer than he; from his shoulders and upwards he was taller than any of the people.
Now, the she-asses of Kish, Shaul's father, became lost, and Kish said to Shaul his son, "Now, take one of the servants and arise and go, seek the she-asses."

And he passed through Mt. Efraim, and he passed through the land of Shalishah, and they did not find them, and they passed through the land of Shaalim and they were not there, and he passed through the land of Binyamin and they did not find them.
When they had come into the land of Tzuf, Shaul said to his servant who was with him, "Come, let us return, lest my father cease to worry about the she-asses, and worry about us."

And he said to him, "Behold now, a man of Elokim is in this city, and the man is held in high esteem; everything which he speaks, surely comes to pass. Now, let us go there; perhaps he will tell us our way upon which we have gone."
And Shaul said to his servant, "And behold, if we go what shall we bring to the man, for the bread is used up from our vessels, and there is no present to bring to the man of Elokim: what have we?"
The lad answered Shaul again, and said, "Behold, I have in my possession a fourth of a shekel of silver, and I shall give it to the man of Elokim, that he may tell us our way."
Formerly, in Yisroel, when a man went to inquire of Elokim, he would say thus, "Come and let us go to the seer," for he who is called a prophet today, was formerly called a seer.
And Shaul said to his servant, "Well said, come, let us go." And they went to the city where the man of Elokim was.
As they were going up the ascent to the city, they found young maidens coming out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"
And they answered them and said, "He is. Behold, he is before you. Hurry now, for today he has come to the city, for the people will have the sacrifice of the day in the high place.

When you come to the city, straightway you will find him, before he ascends the high place to eat, for the people will not eat until he comes, for he will bless the sacrifice, and afterwards the invited guests will eat. Now go up, for at this time, you will find him.
And they went up to the city. As they were coming into the midst of the city, and behold, Shmuel was coming out toward them, to ascend the high place.
Now, Havayah had revealed to Shmuel one day before Shaul's coming, saying,

"At this time tomorrow, I shall send to you a man from the land of Binyamin, and you shall anoint him to be a ruler of my people Yisroel, and he will save My people from the hand of the Pelishtim, for I have looked upon My people, for their cry has come to Me."
And Shmuel saw Shaul, and Havayah said to him, "Behold, the man about whom I said to you, 'This one will rule over My people.' "
And Shaul approached Shmuel inside the gate, and said. "Tell me now, which is the house of the seer?"
And Shmuel answered Shaul, and said, "I am the seer, and you shall eat with me today, and I shall send you away in the morning, and all that is on your mind, I shall tell you.

And concerning the she-asses which are lost to you, today, three days, do not take them to heart, for they have been found; and to whom does all that is desirable in Yisroel belong? Is it not to you and to your father's house?

And Shaul answered and said, "Am I not a Binyamini, of the smallest of the tribes of Yisroel? and my family the least of all the families of Binyamin? Now, why have you spoken to me after this manner?
And Shmuel took Shaul and his servant, and brought them into the chamber, and he gave them a place at the head of the invited guests, who were about thirty men.
And Shmuel said to the cook, "Give the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, 'Keep it with you.' "

And the cook raised up the thigh and that which was upon it, and placed it before Shaul, whereupon he said, "Behold that which has been reserved! Place before you eat, because for the appointed time it is reserved for you, by saying, 'I have invited the people.' " So Shaul ate with Shmuel on that day.
And they descended from the high place to the city, and he spoke with Shaul on the roof.

And they arose early, and it was at dawn, that Shmuel called Shaul to the roof, saying, "Arise and I shall escort you." And Shaul arose, and they went out, both of them, he and Shmuel, into the street.

As they were going down at the outskirts of the city, Shmuel said to Shaul, "Tell the servant to go ahead of us," and he went ahead. "And you, stand still at this time, and I shall let you hear the word of Elokim."
And Shmuel took the vial of oil, and poured it on his head, and kissed him. And he said, "Indeed, Havayah has anointed you to be a ruler over His inheritance.

When you go from me today, you will find two men by Rachel's tomb, in the border of Binyamin, in Zelzah, and they will say to you, The she-asses which you went to seek, were found. And your father had abandoned the matter of the she-asses, and is worried about you, saying, What shall I do about my son?

And you shall go on forward from there, and you shall come to the plain of Tavor, and there will meet you there three men, going up to, to Beit El, one carrying three kids, and one carrying three loaves of bread, and one carrying an earthenware jug of wine.
And they will greet you, and give you two cakes of bread, and you shall take from their hand.

Afterwards, you shall come to the hill of Elokim, where there are Pelishti officers, and it will be, that when you come there to the city, you will meet a band of prophets descending from the high place, and before them will be a psaltery and a drum, and a flute and a harp, and they will prophesy.
And the spirit of Havayah will pass over you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.
And it will be, that when these signs will come to you, do for yourself what your hand will find, for Elokim is with you.

And you shall come down before me to Gilgal, and behold, I shall go down to you to offer up burnt offerings, and to slaughter peace-offerings. Seven days shall you wait until I come to you, and I shall let you know what you shall do."
And it was, when he turned his shoulder to go away from Shmuel, that Elokim gave him another heart, and all these signs came about on that day.
And they came there to the hill, and behold, a band of prophets toward him, and the spirit of Elokim passed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

And it was, that all who had known him before, saw that behold, he was prophesying with the prophets. And the people said to one another, "What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Shaul also among the prophets?"
And a man from there, answered and said, "And who was their father?" It, therefore became a proverb, "Is Shaul also among the prophets?"
And he finished prophesying and came to the high place.
And Shaul's uncle said to him and to his servant, "Where did you go?" And he said, "To seek the she-asses. And when we saw that they were not, we came to Shmuel."
And Shaul's uncle said, "Now tell me what Shmuel said to you."
And Shaul said to his uncle, "He told us that the she-asses had been found," and the matter of the kingdom of which Shmuel had spoken, he did not tell him.
And Shmuel called the people together unto Elokim to Mitzpah.

And he said to the children of Yisroel, "So Havayah said, Elokim of Yisroel, 'I brought Yisroel up from Mitzrayim, and I delivered you from the hand of the Mitzrim, and from the hand of all the kingdoms which oppressed you.'

And today you have rejected your Elokim, Who saves you from all your adversities and your troubles, and you have said to Him, 'But, a king You shall set over us.' And now, stand before Havayah by your tribes and by your thousands."
And Shmuel brought all the tribes of Yisroel near, and the tribe of Binyamin was taken.
And he brought the tribe of Binyamin near, by its families, and the family of the Matrim was taken, and Shaul, the son of Kish, was taken. And they sought him, but he was not found.
And they asked of Havayah further, "Has the man come here yet?" And Havayah said, "Behold, he is hidden among the baggage."
And they ran and took him from there, and he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than all the people from his shoulder and upward.
And Shmuel said to all the people, "Have you seen whom Havayah has chosen, for there is none like him among all the people?" And all the people shouted and said, "Long live the king!"
And Shmuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and he wrote in a book, and placed before Havayah. And Shmuel sent all the people away, each one to his house.
And Shaul too went to his house to Givah, and the band whose heart Elokim had touched, went with him.
And unscrupulous men said, "How will this one save us?" And they despised him and brought him no gift. And he was as one who kept his peace.
And Nachash the Amoni went up and camped against Yavesh-Gilad. And all the people of Yavesh-Gilad said to Nachash, "Make a treaty with us, and we shall serve you."
And Nachash the Amoni said to them, "On this will I make a treaty with you, by gouging out the right eye of every one of you, and I shall make it a reproach against all Yisroel."
And the elders of Yavesh said to him, "Give us seven days respite, that we may send messengers throughout the entire border of Yisroel, and if there is no one to save us, we shall come out to you."
And the messengers came to Givah of Shaul, and spoke the words in the ears of the people. And the people raised their voice and cried.
And behold, Shaul came after the cattle from the field. And Shaul said, "What is troubling the people, that they cry?" And they told him the words of the people of Yavesh.
And a spirit of Elokim passed over Shaul when he heard these words, and his wrath was kindled greatly.

And he took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout the entire border of Yisroel in the hand of the messengers, saying, "Whosoever does not go forth after Shaul and after Shmuel, so shall be done to his oxen," and a fear from Havayah fell upon the people, and they went forth as one man.
And he counted them in Bezek, and the children of Yisroel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Yehudah thirty thousand.

And they said to the messengers who had come, "So shall you say to the people of Yavesh-Gilad, 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will have deliverance.' " And the messengers came and told to the people of Yavesh, and they rejoiced.
And the people of Yavesh said, "Tomorrow we shall come out to you, and you may do to us all that is good in your eyes."

And it was on the morrow, that Shaul put the people into three contingents, and they came into the midst of the camp during the morning watch, and they smote the Amonim until the heat of the day. And it was, that those remaining, scattered, and no two of them remained together.
And the people said to Shmuel, "Whosoever says, 'Shaul will reign over us?' give over the people and let us put them to death. "
And Shaul said, "No man shall be put to death on this day, for today, Havayah has wrought deliverance in Yisroel."
And Shmuel said to the people, "Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew there the kingdom."
And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Shaul king before Havayah in Gilgal, and there they slaughtered peace-offerings before Havayah, and Shaul and all the people rejoiced greatly.
And Shmuel said to all Yisroel, "Behold, I have hearkened to your voice, to everything which you have said to me, and I have made a king to reign over you.
And now, behold the king is walking before you, and I have become old and hoary, and my sons are here with you, and I have walked before you from my youth and until this day.

Here I am; bear witness against me before Havayah and before His anointed; whose ox did I take, or whose ass did I take, or whom did I rob; or whom did I oppress, or from whose hand did I take a ransom, that I hide my eyes therewith, and I shall restore to you."
And they said, "You did not rob us, nor did you oppress us, neither did you take anything from anyone's hand."
And he said to them, "Havayah is a witness against you, and His anointed is witness this day, that you have not found anything in my hand, and they said, " witness."
And Shmuel said to the people, " Havayah Who made Moshe and Aharon, and Who brought your forefathers up from the land of Mitzrayim.
And now, stand and I shall reason with you before Havayah, concerning all the righteous acts which He did to you and to your forefathers.
When Yackov came to Mitzrayim, and your forefathers cried out to Havayah, Havayah sent Moshe and Aharon, and they brought your forefathers out of Mitzrayim, and they made them dwell in this place.

And they forgot Havayah, their Elokim, and He delivered them into the hand of Sisera, the commander of the army of Chatzor, and into the hand of the Pelishtim, and into the hand of the king of Moav, and they waged war with them.
And they cried out to Havayah, and said, 'We have sinned, for we have forsaken Havayah, and have served the Be'alim and Ashtarot. Now, save us from the hand of our enemies, and we shall serve You.'
And Havayah sent Yerubaal, and Bedan, and Yeftah, and Shmuel, and He saved you from the hand of your enemies round about, and you dwelt in safety.
And when you saw that Nachash, the king of Amon, came upon you, you said to me, 'No, but a king shall rule over us,' when Havayah your Elokim was your king.
And now, behold the king whom you have chosen, whom you have requested, and behold, Havayah has appointed a king over you.

If you will fear Havayah, and serve Him, and hearken to His voice, and you will not rebel against the commandments of Havayah, both you and the king who reigns over you, will be after Havayah your Elokim.
But, if you will not hearken to the voice of Havayah, and you will rebel against the commandments of Havayah, Havayah's hand will be against you and against your fathers.
Even now, stand and see this great thing which Havayah will do before your eyes.

Is it not wheat harvest today? I shall call out to Havayah, and He will send thunder and rain, and you shall know and see, that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of Havayah, to ask for yourselves a king."
And Shmuel called out to Havayah, and Havayah sent thunder and rain on that day, and all the people greatly feared Havayah and Shmuel.
And all the people said to Shmuel, "Pray for your servants to Havayah your Elokim and let us not die, for we have added to all our sins evil, to ask for ourselves a king."
And Shmuel said to the people, "Fear not. You have done all this evil, but do not turn aside from following Havayah, and you shall serve Havayah with all your heart.
And you shall not turn aside, for then after vain things which cannot profit or deliver, for they are vain.
For Havayah will not forsake His people for His great name's sake; for Havayah has sworn to make you a people for Himself.
I also, far be it from me to sin to Havayah in ceasing to pray for you, but I shall instruct you in the good and proper way.
Only fear Havayah and you shall serve Him in truth with all your heart, for see the great things which He has dealt with you.
But, if you will do wrong, both you and your king will be destroyed.
Shaul was a year in his reign, and he reigned two years over Yisroel.

And Shaul chose for himself three thousand from Yisroel, and they were with Shaul; two thousand in Michmas and in the mountain of Beit El, and one thousand were with Yehonatan in Givah of Binyamin, and he sent the rest of the people, every man to his tents.
And Yehonatan smote the officer of the Pelishtim, who was in Geva, and the Pelishtim heard; and Shaul sounded the shofar throughout all the land, saying: "Let the Ivrim hear."
And all Yisroel heard, saying, "Shaul has smitten the officer of the Pelishtim, and also that Yisroel has become hateful to the Pelishtim." And the people gathered after Shaul to Gilgal.

And the Pelishtim gathered to wage war with Yisroel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand riders, and people as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and they went up and camped in Michmas to the east of Beit-Aven.
And the men of Yisroel saw that they were in a strait, for the people were hard-pressed, and the people hid in the caves, and in the thickets, in the rocky crags, and in the towers, and in the pits.
And some Ivrim crossed the Yarden to the land of Gad and Gilad, but Shaul was still in Gilgal, and all the people hurried after him.
And he waited seven days, to the appointed time which Shmuel, and Shmuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people scattered from him.
And Shaul said, "Bring near to me the burnt offering and the peace offering"; and he offered up the burnt offering.
And it was, when he finished offering up the burnt offering, that behold, Shmuel came, and Shaul went out toward him to greet him.

And Shmuel said, "What have you done?" And Shaul said, "For I saw that the people had scattered from me, and you did not come at the appointed time of the days, and the Pelishtim are gathered in Michmas.
And I said, 'Now the Pelishtim will come down against me to Gilgal, and I have not yet made supplication before Havayah,' and I forced myself, and I offered up the burnt offering."

And Shmuel said to Shaul, "You have done foolishly; you have not observed the commandment of Havayah your Elokim, which He commanded you, for now, Havayah would have established your kingdom over Yisroel forever.

But now, your kingdom shall not continue; Havayah has sought for Himself a man after His heart, and Havayah has appointed him to be a ruler over His people, for you have not kept that which Havayah commanded you."
And Shmuel rose and went up from Gilgal to Givah of Binyamin; and Shaul counted the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
And Shaul and his son Yehonatan and the people who were present with them were staying in Geva of Binyamin, while the Pelishtim were encamped in Michmas.
And the raiders emerged from the camp of the Pelishtim in three companies; one company turned to the road to Ofrah, to the land of Shual.
And one company turned to the road leading to Beit-Choron, and one company turned to the road leading to the border, which overlooks the valley of the 'zeboim', toward the wilderness.
Now, not a smith was to be found in all the land of Yisroel, for the Pelishtim said, "Lest the Ivrim make sword or spear."
And all Yisroel went down to the the Pelishtim to sharpen each man his plowshare and his colter and his axe and his mattock.
And there was a file for the mattocks and for the colters and for the three-pronged pitchforks and for the axes, and to set the goad.
And it was on the day of war, that neither sword nor spear was found in the possession of all the people who were with Shaul and with Yehonatan, but Shaul and Yehonatan his son had them.
And the garrison of the Pelishtim went out to the other side of Michmas.

And it came to pass one day, that Yehonatan the son of Shaul said to the youth who bore his weapons, "Come, and let us cross to the garrison of the Pelishtim which is on the other side yonder." But he did not tell his father.
Now Shaul was staying in the outskirts of Givah, under the pomegranate tree which was in Migron, and the people who were with him, were about six hundred men.
And Ahiah, the son of Achituv, the brother of I-Kavod, the son of Pinchas, the son of Eli, the priest of Havayah in Shilo, wearing an ephod; and the people did not know that Yehonatan had gone.

And between the sides which Yehonatan sought to cross to the garrison of the Pelishtim, there was a rocky crag from this side, and a rocky crag from this side; the name of one being Botzetz, and the name of the other being Seneh.
One crag was situated from the north, opposite Michmas, and one opposite Geva.

And Yehonatan said to the youth, who bore his weapons, "Come, and let us go to the garrison of these uncircumcised; perhaps Havayah will act on our behalf, for with Havayah there is no limitation to save with many or with few."
And his weapon-bearer said to him, "Do all that is in your heart. Turn to you. Behold, I am with you according to your heart."
And Yehonatan said, "Behold, we are crossing to the men, and we shall reveal ourselves to them.
If they say thus to us, 'Wait! Until we reach you,' then we shall stand in our place, and we shall not go up to them.
And if they say thus, 'Come up to us,' then we shall go up, for Havayah has given them into our hand, and this will be the sign for us."
And both of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Pelishtim, and the Pelishtim said, "Behold, Ivrim are emerging from the holes wherein they hid themselves."

And the men of the garrison called Yehonatan and his weapon-bearer, and said, "Come up to us, and we shall tell you something." And Yehonatan said to his weapon- bearer, "Come up after me, for Havayah has given them into the hand of Yisroel."
And Yehonatan climbed up on his hands and on his feet, with his weapon-bearer after him, and they fell before Yehonatan, and his weapon-bearer was slaying after him.
And the first slaughter which Yehonatan and his weapon-bearer made, was about twenty men, in about half a furrow a yoke a field.
And there was a trembling in the camp and the field, and among the people; the garrison and the raiders also trembled, and the earth quaked and became a trembling inspired by Elokim.
And Shaul's lookouts in Givah of Binyamin, and behold the multitude was wandering, and it was coming closer.
And Shaul said to the people who were with him, "Inspect now, and see who is gone from among us." And they inspected, and behold, Yehonatan and his weapon-bearer were not there.
And Shaul said to Ahiah, "Bring near the Ark of Elokim," for the Ark of Elokim was on that day with the children of Yisroel.
And it was, while Shaul still spoke to the priest, that the tumult which was in the camp of the Pelishtim was continuously increasing, and Shaul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."
And Shaul and all the people who were with him, gathered, and came to the battle, and behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, a very great confusion.
And the Ivrim were with the Pelishtim as previously, who went up with them in the camp round about, they too to be with the Bnei Yisroel who were with Shaul and Yehonatan.
And all the people who were hiding in Mt. Efraim, heard that the Pelishtim had fled, and they too pursued closely behind them in the battle.
And Havayah saved Yisroel on that day, and the battle passed Beit-Aven.

And the men of Yisroel were hard pressed on that day, and Shaul adjured the people, saying, "Cursed be the man who will eat food until evening, until I shall be avenged of my enemies," and none of the people tasted any food.
And all the land came in the forest, and there was honey on the ground.
And the people came into the forest, and behold, a flow of honey, but no one put his hand to his mouth for the people feared the oath.

But Yehonatan had not heard when his father had adjured the people, and he extended the end of the staff which was in his hand, and dipped it into the honeycomb, and when he brought back his hand to his mouth, his eyes brightened.
And one man of the people called out and said, "Your father adjured the people, saying, 'Cursed be the man who eats food today,' and the people have become faint."
And Yehonatan said, "My father has perturbed the land. See now that my eyes have brightened, for I have tasted a little of this honey.
How much more, if the people had eaten today of the spoils of their enemies, which they found, would there not now have been a greater slaughter among the Pelishtim?"
And they smote the Pelishtim that day, from Michmas to Ayalon, and the people became very faint.
And the people flew to the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and they slaughtered on the ground, and the people ate with the blood.
And they told Shaul, saying, "Behold, the people are sinning against Havayah, by eating with the blood." And he said, "You have transgressed; roll a huge stone to me this day."

And Shaul said, "Disperse among the people, and you shall say to them, 'Bring near to me each man his ox and each man his lamb, and you shall slaughter here, and you shall eat, and you shall not sin against Havayah by eating with the blood.' " And all the people brought near, each man his ox that night, and they slaughtered there.
And Shaul built an altar to Havayah; with that one he started to build an altar to Havayah.

And Shaul said, "Let us go down after the Pelishtim at night, and plunder among them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man among them. " And they said, "Do all that is good in your eyes." Whereupon the priest said, "Let us draw near here to Elokim."
And Shaul asked of Elokim, "Shall I go down after the Pelishtim? Will you deliver them into the hand of Yisroel?" But He did not answer him on that day.
And Shaul said, "Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see wherein was this sin today.
For as Havayah lives, who saves Yisroel, for though it be in Yehonatan my son, he will die," and there was no one who answered him from among all the people.
And he said to all Yisroel, "You will be to one side, and I and my son Yehonatan will be to one side." And the people answered Shaul, "Do what is good in your eyes."
And Shaul said to Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, "Give a perfect lot," whereupon Yehonatan and Shaul were taken, and the people escaped.
And Shaul said, "Cast lots between me and Yehonatan my son;" and Yehonatan was taken.
And Shaul said to Yehonatan, "Tell me; what have you done?" And Yehonatan told him and said, "I but tasted a bit of honey with the end of the staff which is in my hand. Here I am; let me die."
And Shaul said, "So shall Elokim do, and so shall He continue; for you shall die, Yehonatan."

And the people said to Shaul, "Shall Yehonatan, who has wrought this great salvation in Yisroel, die? Far be it. As Havayah lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has worked with Elokim this day." And the people redeemed Yehonatan, and he did not die.
And Shaul went up from after the Pelishtim, and the Pelishtim went to their place.

And Shaul took the kingdom over Yisroel, and he waged war against his enemies on every side, against Moav, and against the children of Amon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Tzovah, and against the Pelishtim, and wherever he would turn, he would cause them to tremble.
And he gathered an army, and he smote Amalek, and he saved Yisroel from the hand of its plunderer.
And the sons of Shaul were Yehonatan, and Yishvi, and Malkishua; and the names of his daughters, the name of the firstborn was Merav, and the name of the younger was Michal.
And the name of Shaul's wife was Achinoam, the daughter of Achima'atz; and the name of the commander of his army was Avner, the son of Ner, Shaul's uncle.
And Kish, the father of Shaul, and Ner, the father of Avner, were sons of Aviel.
And the war against the Pelishtim was severe all the days of Shaul; when Shaul saw any valiant man or any soldierly man, he would bring him in to himself.
And Shmuel said to Shaul, "Havayah sent me to anoint you to be king over His people, over Yisroel; and now hearken to the voice of the words of Havayah.
So Havayah said of Hosts, 'I remember that which Amalek did to Yisroel, how he laid for him on the way, when he came up out of Mitzrayim.

Now, go, and you shall smite Amalek, and you shall utterly destroy all that is his, and you shall not have pity on him: and you shall slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.' "
And Shaul called the people together, and he counted them in Tela'im, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand, the men of Yehudah.
And Shaul came as far as the city of Amalek, and he fought in the valley.

And Shaul said to the Keini, "Turn away and go down from among the Amalekim, lest I destroy you with them, and you did kindness with all the children of Yisroel, when they went up out of Mitzrayim." And the Keinim turned away from amidst Amalek.
And Shaul smote Amalek, from Chavilah until you come to Shur, which is in front of Mitzrayim.
And he seized Agag, the king of Amalek, alive; and he completely destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.

And Shaul and the people had pity on Agag, and on the best of the sheep and the cattle, and the fatlings, and on the fattened sheep, and on all that was good; and they did not want to destroy them; but everything which was vile and feeble, that they utterly destroyed.
And the word of Havayah came to Shmuel, saying,
"I regret that I have made Shaul king, for he has turned back from following Me, and he has not fulfilled My words." And it distressed Shmuel, and he cried out to Havayah all night.

And Shmuel arose early in the morning to meet Shaul; and it was told to Shmuel, saying, "Shaul has come to Karmel, and behold, he is setting up a place for himself, and he passed and went down to Gilgal."
And Shmuel came to Shaul, and Shaul said to him, "May you be blessed of Havayah; I have fulfilled the word of Havayah."
And Shmuel said, "What then is this bleating of the sheep in my ears? And the lowing of the oxen which I hear?"

And Shaul said, "They brought them from the Amalekim, for the people had pity on the best of the sheep, and the oxen, in order to sacrifice to Havayah your Elokim: and the rest we have utterly destroyed."
And Shmuel said to Shaul, "Desist, and I shall tell you what Havayah spoke to me last night." And he said to him, "Speak."
And Shmuel said, "Even if you are small in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Yisroel? And Havayah anointed you as king over Yisroel.
And Havayah sent you on a mission, and said, 'Go, and you shall utterly destroy the sinners, the Amalekim, and you shall wage war against them until they destroy them.'
Now, why did you not hearken to the voice of Havayah, but you flew upon the spoil, and you did what was evil in the eyes of Havayah?"

And Shaul said to Shmuel, "Yes, I did hearken to the voice of Havayah. I did go on the mission on which Havayah sent me, and I brought Agag, the king of Amalek alive, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekim.
And the people took from the spoil, sheep and oxen, the best of the ban, to sacrifice to your Elokim in Gilgal."
And Shmuel said, "Has Havayah desire in burnt offerings and peace-offerings, as in obeying the voice of Havayah? Behold, to obey is better than a peace-offering; to hearken than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Since you rejected the word of Havayah, He has rejected you from being a king."
And Shaul said to Shmuel, "I have sinned, for I transgressed Havayah's command, and your words, for I feared the people, and I hearkened to their voice.
And now, forgive now my sin, and return with me, and I shall prostrate myself to Havayah."
And Shmuel said to Shaul, "I shall not return with you, for you have rejected the word of Havayah, and Havayah has rejected you from being a king over Yisroel."
And Shmuel turned to go, and he seized the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
And Shmuel said to him, "Havayah has torn the kingdom of Yisroel from you, today; and has given it to your fellow who is better than you.
And also, the Strength of Yisroel will neither lie nor repent, for He is not a man to repent."
And he said, "I have sinned. Now, honor me now in the presence of the elders of my people, and in the presence of Yisroel, and return with me, and I shall prostrate myself to Havayah your Elokim."
And Shmuel returned after Shaul, and Shaul prostrated himself to Havayah.
And Shmuel said, "Bring Agag, the king of Amalek, near to me." And Agag went to him delicately. And Agag said, "Surely, the bitterness of death has turned."
And Shmuel said, "As your sword bereaved women, so will your mother be bereaved among women." And Shmuel hewed Agag in pieces before Havayah in Gilgal.
And Shmuel went to Ramah, and Shaul went up to his house in Givah of Shaul.
And Shmuel came no more to see Shaul until the day of his death, for Shmuel mourned for Shaul, and Havayah was repentant that He had made Shaul reign over Yisroel.

And Havayah said to Shmuel, "Until when are you mourning for Shaul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Yisroel? Fill your horn with oil, and come, I shall send you to Yishai, the Beit-Lechemi, for I have seen for Myself a king among his sons."
And Shmuel said, "How shall I go? For, if Shaul hears, he will kill me." And Havayah said, "You shall take a heifer with you, and you shall say, 'I have come to slaughter to Havayah.'
And you shall invite Yishai to the sacrificial feast, and I shall let you know what you shall do, and you shall anoint for Me whom I shall tell you."
And Shmuel did that which Havayah had spoken, and he came to Beit Lechem, and the elders of the city hurried toward him, and one said, "Is your coming peaceable?"

And he said, "Peaceable. I have come to slaughter to Havayah. Prepare yourselves, and you shall come with me to the sacrificial feast." And he prepared Yishai and his sons, and invited them to the sacrificial feast.
And it was, that when they came, and he saw Eliav, that he said, "Surely, before Havayah is His anointed."
And Havayah said to Shmuel, "Look not upon his appearance, or the height of his stature, for I have rejected him, for it is not as man sees, to the eyes, while Havayah sees into the heart."
And Yishai called Avinadav, and he presented him before Shmuel, and he said, "Neither has Havayah chosen this one."
And Yishai presented Shamah, and he said, "Neither has Havayah chosen this one."
And Yishai presented his seven sons before Shmuel; and Shmuel said to Yishai, "Havayah has not chosen these."

And Shmuel said to Yishai, "Are these all the young men?" And he said, "The youngest still remains, and behold, he is tending the sheep." And Shmuel said to Yishai, "Send and bring him, for we shall not sit down until he comes here."
And he sent and brought him, and he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and handsome appearance. And Havayah said, "Arise, anoint him, for this is he."
And Shmuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And a spirit of Havayah passed over Dovid from that day forth, and Shmuel arose and went to Ramah.
And the spirit of Havayah departed from Shaul, and an evil spirit from Havayah frightened him.
And Shaul's servants said to him, "Behold now, an evil spirit of Elokim is frightening you.
Let our master say, 'Let them seek a man who knows how to play on the harp'; and it will be, that when the evil spirit of Elokim is upon you, he will play with his hand, and it will be good for you."
And Shaul said to his servants, "Provide me now with a man who plays well, and you shall bring him to me."

And one of the young men answered and said, "Behold, I saw a son of Yishai the Beit-Lechemi, who knows how to play, a mighty man of valor, and a warrior, and prudent in affairs, and a handsome man, and Havayah is with him."
And Shaul sent messengers to Yishai, and he said, "Send me Dovid your son, who is with the sheep."
And Yishai took a donkey laden with bread, and an earthenware jug of wine, and a kid; and he sent them with Dovid his son, to Shaul.
And Dovid came to Shaul, and stood before him, and he loved him very much, and he was his weapon bearer.
And Shaul sent to Yishai, saying, "Let Dovid stand before me now, for he has found favor in my eyes."

And it would be, that when the spirit of Elokim was upon Shaul, that Dovid would take the harp, and would play with his hand, and Shaul would be relieved, and it would be good for him, the spirit of evil would depart from him.
And the Pelishtim assembled their camps to war; and they assembled at Sochoh which belonged to Yehudah, and they encamped between Sochoh and Azekah in Efes-Damim.
And Shaul and the men of Yisroel assembled, and they encamped in the Valley of the Terebinth, and they set the battle in array against the Pelishtim.
And the Pelishtim were standing on the mountain from here, and Yisroel was standing on the mountain from here, and the valley was between them.
And the champion emerged from the Pelishtim' camp, named Golyat, from Gat; his height was six cubits and a span.
And a helmet of copper was on his head, and he was wearing a coat of mail, and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of copper.
And greaves of copper were on his legs, and a copper javelin was between his shoulders.
And the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the spear's head was six hundred shekels of iron, and the shield-bearer went before him.

And he stood and called the array of Yisroel, and he said to them, "Why should you come out to wage war? Am I not the Pelishti, and you the servants of Shaul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me.
If he is able to fight with me and kill me, we shall be slaves to you, and if I overcome him, and kill him, you shall be slaves to us and serve us."
And the Pelishti said, "I taunt the ranks of Yisroel this day; give me a man, and let us fight together."
And Shaul and all Yisroel heard these words of the Pelishti, and they were panic stricken and very much afraid.
And Dovid was the son of this Efrati man from Beit Lechem of Yehudah, whose name was Yishai; and he had eight sons; and the man was old in Shaul's time, coming among men.

And Yishai's three eldest sons who had followed Shaul, went to war; and the names of his three sons who went to war, were: Eliav, the firstborn, and the second to him, Avinadav, and the third, Shamah.
And Dovid was the youngest, and the three eldest followed Shaul.
Now Dovid went to and fro from Shaul, to tend his father's sheep in Beit Lechem.
And the Pelishti drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
And Yishai said to Dovid his son, "Take now to your brothers, an ephah of this parched corn and ten loaves of this bread, and rush them to the camp, to your brothers.
And you shall bring these ten cheeses to the captain of the thousand, and you shall see how your brothers are faring, and you shall take the tidings of their welfare."
And Shaul and they, and all the men of Yisroel in the Valley of the Terebinth, were at war with the Pelishtim.

And Dovid arose early in the morning, and he left the sheep with a keeper; and he carried off and went, as Yishai had commanded him; and he came to the barricade, and the army which was going out to the battle array, shouted in the battle.
And the Bnei Yisroel and the Pelishtim put the battle in array, army against army.
And Dovid left the baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and he ran to the battle array, and he came and greeted his brothers.
And while he was speaking with them, behold, the champion, named Golyat the Pelishti, from Gat, was coming up from the ranks of the Pelishtim, and he spoke the same words, and Dovid heard.
And all the men of Yisroel, upon seeing the man, fled from before him, and were exceedingly frightened.

And the men of Yisroel said, "Have you seen this man who is coming up, for he is coming up to taunt Yisroel? And it will be, that the man who will kill him, the King will enrich him with great riches, and he will give him his daughter, and he will make his father's house free in Yisroel."

And Dovid said to the men who were standing before him, saying, "What shall be done to the man who slays that Pelishti, and takes away reproach from Yisroel, for who is this uncircumcised Pelishti, that he should taunt the ranks of the living Elokim?"
And the people said to him, "So shall be done to the man who slays him."

And Eliav, his eldest brother, heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliav's wrath was kindled against Dovid, and he said, "Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the desert? I know your impetuousness, and the evil of your heart, for you have come down in order to see the war."
And Dovid said, "What have I done now? Is it not but a word?"
And he turned around from him, toward another. And he spoke according to the same manner, the people answered according to the former manner.
And the words which Dovid had spoken, were heard. And they related before Shaul, and he took him.
And Dovid said to Shaul, "Let no man's heart fail because of him. Your bondsman will go, and battle with the Pelishti."
And Shaul said to Dovid, "You are unable to go to this Pelishti to battle with him, for you are a lad, and he is a warrior since his youth."
And Dovid said to Shaul, "Your bondsman was a shepherd of sheep for his father, and there came a lion and also a bear, and carried off a lamb from the flock.
And I went out after him and smote him, and saved it from his mouth. And he arose upon me, and I took hold of his jaw, and I smote him and slew him.
Both the lion and the bear has your bondsman slain, and the uncircumcised Pelishti shall be like one of them, for he taunted the armies of the living Elokim."

And Dovid said, "Havayah Who saved me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, He will save me from the hand of this Pelishti." And Shaul said to Dovid, "Go, and may Havayah be with you."
And Shaul dressed Dovid with his garments, and he placed a copper helmet on his head, and he dressed him with a coat of mail.

And Dovid girded his sword over his garments, and he did not want to go, for he was not accustomed, and Dovid said to Shaul, "I cannot go with these, for I am not accustomed." And Dovid took them off.

And he took his staff in his hand, and he chose for himself five smooth pebbles from the brook, and he placed them in the shepherds' bag which he had, and in the sack, and his slingshot was in his hand, and he approached the Pelishti.
And the Pelishti was continuously drawing nearer to Dovid, and the man who bore the shield was before him.
And the Pelishti looked and saw Dovid, and he despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy, with an attractive appearance.
And the Pelishti said to Dovid, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?" And the Pelishti cursed Dovid by his deity.
And the Pelishti said to Dovid, "Come to me, and I shall give your flesh to the fowl of the air, and to the cattle of the field."
And Dovid said to the Pelishti, "You come to me with sword, spear and javelin, and I come to you with the Name of Havayah of Hosts, Elokim of the armies of Yisroel which you have taunted.

This day, Havayah will deliver you into my hand, and I shall slay you, and take off your head, and I shall give the carcasses of the camp of the Pelishtim this day, to the fowl of the air and to the beasts of the earth, and all the earth shall know that Yisroel has an Elokim.
And all this assembly shall know that not with sword and javelin does Havayah save, for the battle is Havayah's, and He will deliver you into our hand."
And it was, when the Pelishti arose and drew closer to Dovid, that Dovid hastened and ran to the battle array, toward the Pelishti.

And Dovid stretched his hand into the bag, and took a stone therefrom, and slung it, and he hit the Pelishti in his forehead, and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
And Dovid overpowered the Pelishti with the slingshot and with the stone, and he smote the Pelishti and slew him: and no sword was in Dovid's hand.

And Dovid ran and stood up to the Pelishti, and he took his sword and drew it from its sheath, and slew him, and with it, severed his head. And the Pelishtim saw that their hero had died, and they fled.

And the men of Yisroel and Yehudah arose and shouted, and pursued the Pelishtim until you come to the valley, and until the Gates of Ekron; and the slain of the Pelishtim fell on the road of Shaaraim, and up to Gat and up to Ekron.
And the children of Yisroel returned from pursuing the Pelishtim, and plundered their camps.
And Dovid took the head of the Pelishti, and brought it to Yerushalayim, and his weapons, he put in his tent.
And when Shaul saw Dovid going out toward the Pelishti, he said to Avner, the general of his army, "Whose son is this youth, Avner?" And Avner said, "By your life, O King, I know not."
And the king said, "You ask whose son this youth is."
And as Dovid returned from slaying the Pelishti, Avner called him, and brought him before Shaul, and the Pelishti's head was in his hand.
And Shaul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" And Dovid said, "The son of your bondsman, Yishai the Beit-Lechemi."
And it was, as he finished speaking to Shaul, that Yehonatan's soul had become attached to Dovid's soul, and Yehonatan loved him as himself.
And Shaul took him on that day, and did not allow him to return to his father's house.
And Yehonatan made a covenant with Dovid because he loved him as himself.
And Yehonatan stripped himself of the cloak which was on him, and gave it to Dovid, and his garments, even to his sword, and even to his bow, and even to his girdle.

And Dovid went out; wherever Shaul would send him, he would succeed; accordingly, Shaul appointed him over the soldiers, and he was pleasing in the eyes of all the people, and also in the eyes of Shaul's servants.

And it was when they came, when Dovid returned from slaying the Pelishti, that the women came out of all the cities of Yisroel, to sing, and with musical instruments, toward King Shaul, with drums, with joy, and with cymbals.
And the cheering women sang out and said, "Shaul has slain his thousands, and Dovid his ten thousands."
And Shaul was very chagrined, and the matter displeased him, and he said, "They ascribed to Dovid ten thousands, and to me they ascribed the thousands. And what more can he have, but the kingdom?"
And Shaul eyed Dovid from that day on.

And it was on the morrow, that the evil spirit from Elokim rested upon Shaul, and he raved in the midst of the house, and Dovid was playing with his hand like everyday, and the spear was in Shaul's hand.
And Shaul cast the spear, and said, "I shall pin Dovid to the wall," and Dovid turned from before him twice.
And Shaul feared Dovid, for Havayah was with him, while He had turned away from Shaul.
And Shaul removed him from with him, and made him for himself a captain over a thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.
And Dovid was successful in all his ways; and Havayah was with him.
And Shaul saw that he was very successful, and he feared him.
And all Yisroel and Yehudah loved Dovid, for he went out and came in before them.

And Shaul said to Dovid, "Behold, my elder daughter, Merav. I shall give her to you as a wife. But, be a warrior for me, and wage the wars of Havayah." For Shaul said, "Let not my hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Pelishtim be upon him."
And Dovid said to Shaul, "Who am I, and what is my life, or my fathers family in Yisroel, that I should be a son-in-law to the King."
And it was at the time that Merav, Shaul's daughter, should have been given to Dovid, that she was given to Adriel, the Mecholati, as a wife.
And Michal, Shaul's daughter, loved Dovid; and they told Shaul, and the thing pleased him.
And Shaul said, "I shall give her to him, and she will be a snare to him, and the hand of the Pelishtim will be upon him." And Shaul said to Dovid, "With two, shall you be my son-in-law today."
And Shaul commanded his servants, "Speak to Dovid secretly, saying, 'Behold, the king desires you, and all his servants love you; and now, become the king's son-in-law.' "
And Shaul's servants spoke these words in Dovid's ears. And Dovid said, "Does becoming the king's son-in-law, seem to you to be a light thing, for I am poor and lightly esteemed?"
And Shaul's servants told him, saying, "According to these words, has Dovid spoken."

And Shaul said, "So shall you say to Dovid, 'The king has no desire in a dowry, but in one hundred foreskins of Pelishtim, to avenge himself upon the king's enemies.' " But Shaul thought to make Dovid fall by the hand of the Pelishtim.
And his servants told Dovid these words, and the thing pleased Dovid to become the king's son-in-law, and the days had not expired.

And Dovid arose, and he and his men went, and he slew two hundred men of the Pelishtim, and brought their foreskins, and they delivered them in full to the king, in order to become the king's son-in-law. And the king gave him Michal, his daughter, as a wife.
And Shaul saw, and knew that Havayah was with Dovid, and Michal, Shaul's daughter, loved him.
And Shaul grew still more afraid of Dovid, and Shaul was hostile to Dovid all the days.
And the princes of the Pelishtim came out, and it was, as often as they came out, that Dovid was more successful than all Shaul's servants, and his name was highly esteemed.
And Shaul spoke to Yehonatan his son and to all his servants to put Dovid to death. But Yehonatan, Shaul's son, desired Dovid very much.
And Yehonatan told Dovid, saying, "Shaul, my father, seeks to put you to death, and now, beware now in the morning, and you shall remain in secret, and hide.
And I shall come out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I shall speak on your behalf to my father; and if I see something, I shall tell you."

And Yehonatan spoke well of Dovid to Shaul, his father, and he said to him, "Let not the king sin against his servant Dovid, because he has not sinned against you, and because his deeds are very good toward you.

And he put his life in his hand and slew the Pelishti, and Havayah wrought a great salvation for all Yisroel. You saw and rejoiced. Why, then, should you sin against innocent blood, to put Dovid to death for no reason?"
And Shaul listened to Yehonatan's voice, and Shaul swore, "As Havayah lives, he will not be put to death."
And Yehonatan called Dovid, and Yehonatan told him all these things. And Yehonatan brought Dovid to Shaul, and he was before him as yesterday and before.
And there was war again, and Dovid went out and battled the Pelishtim, and dealt a great blow upon them, and they fled from before him.
And an evil spirit from Havayah was upon Shaul, and he was sitting in his house, with his spear in his hand, and Dovid was playing with his hand.
And Shaul attempted to pin Dovid to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from before Shaul, and Shaul drove the spear into the wall, but Dovid fled and escaped on that night.

And Shaul sent messengers to Dovid's house to guard him and to put him to death in the morning, and Michal his wife told Dovid, saying, "If you do not flee for your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death!"
And Michal let Dovid down through the window, and he went, and fled, and escaped.
And Michal took the teraphim, and put them into the bed, and she put a goatskin at its head, and covered it with a garment.
And Shaul sent messengers to take Dovid, and she said, "He is ill."
And Shaul sent the messengers to see Dovid, saying, "Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may put him to death."
And the messengers came, and behold, the teraphim was in the bed, and the goatskin was at its head.
And Shaul said to Michal, "Why have you thus deceived me, and you sent away my enemy, so that he escaped?" And Michal said to Shaul, "He said to me, 'Let me go. Why should I put you to death?' "
Now Dovid had fled and escaped, and he came to Shmuel to Ramah, and told him all that Shaul had done to him, and he and Shmuel went and stayed in Nayot.
And it was related to Shaul, saying, "Behold, Dovid is at Nayot in Ramah."
