And Shaul sent messengers to take Dovid, and he saw the company of prophets prophesying and Shmuel was standing as head over them; and a spirit from Elokim was upon Shaul's messengers, and they too prophesied.
And they told Shaul, and he sent other messengers, and they too prophesied. And Shaul continued to send third messengers, and they too prophesied.
And he also went to Ramah, and he came to the great pit which is in Secu, and he asked, and said, "Where are Shmuel and Dovid?" And said, "Behold, at Nayot in Ramah."
And he went there, to Nayot in Ramah, and even upon him was a spirit from Elokim, and he went along prophesying until he came to Nayot in Ramah.
And he too stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied before Shmuel, and he fell naked all that day and all the night. Therefore, they say, "Is Shaul also among the prophets?"
And Dovid fled from Nayot in Ramah, and he came and said before Yehonatan, "What have I done? What is my transgression and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?"
And he said to him, "Far be it. You shall not die. My father will do nothing, either great or small, that he will not reveal to me. And why should my father conceal this thing from me? It is not "

And Dovid swore further, and said, "Your father knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he said, 'Let not Yehonatan know this, lest he become saddened.' But, indeed, as Havayah lives, and by the life of your soul, there is but a step between me and death."
And Yehonatan said to Dovid, "What your soul will say, I shall do for you."

And Dovid said to Yehonatan, "Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I am accustomed to sit with the king, to eat. And you shall let me go, that I may hide in the field until the evening of the third day.
If your father is mindful of me, you shall say, 'Dovid took leave of me to hasten home to Beit Lechem, his city, for it is the yearly sacrifice there for the whole family.'
If he says thus, 'Good,' then it is well with your bondsman, but if he becomes angry, know that the evil has been decided upon by him.

And you shall do kindness with your bondsman, for into the covenant of Havayah, have you brought your bondsman with you, and if there be guilt in me, put me to death yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?"
And Yehonatan said, "Far be it from you. For if I know that the evil has been decided upon by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you that?"
And Dovid said to Yehonatan, "Who will tell me, or what your father will answer you harshly?"
And Yehonatan said to Dovid, "Come, and let us go out to the field." And both of them went out to the field.

And Yehonatan said to Dovid, " Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, that I shall sound out my father at this time on the third morrow, and behold, if it is good for Dovid, will I not send for you then, and reveal it to you?

So shall Havayah do to Yehonatan and more also, if it pleases my father to evil upon you, I shall reveal it to you, and I shall send you away, that you may go in peace, and may Havayah be with you as He was with my father.
And I shall not ask of you if I am still alive, will you not do kindness of Havayah with me, that I die not?
And you shall not discontinue your kindness from my household forever, and not even when Havayah cuts off Dovid's enemies, each man from upon the face of the earth."
And Yehonatan made a covenant with the house of Dovid, "And may Havayah demand it from the hand of Dovid's enemies."
And Yehonatan continued to make Dovid swear, in his love for him, for he loved him the love of his soul.
And Yehonatan said to him, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be remembered, for your seat will be vacant.
And for three days, you shall hide very well, and you shall come to the place where you hid on the day of work, and you shall stay beside the traveler's stone.
And I shall shoot three arrows to the side, as though I shot at a mark.

And behold, I shall send the youth, 'Go, find the arrows.' If I say to the youth, 'Behold, the arrows are on this side of you,' take it and come, for it is well with you, and there is nothing the matter, as Havayah lives.
But, if I say thus to the youth, 'Behold, the arrows are beyond you,' go! For Havayah has sent you away.
And the matter which we have spoken, I and you, behold, Havayah is between me and you forever."
And Dovid hid in the field, and when it was the new moon, Shaul sat down to the meal to eat.
And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, upon the seat by the wall, and Yehonatan arose, and Avner sat down beside Shaul, and Dovid's place was vacant.
And Shaul did not say anything on that day, for he thought, "It is an incident; he is not clean, for he is not clean."
And it was, on the morrow of the new moon, the second, that Dovid's place was vacant, and Shaul said to Yehonatan, his son, "Why has not the son of Yishai come to the meal either yesterday or today?"
And Yehonatan answered Shaul, "Dovid asked leave of me to Beit Lechem.

And he said, 'Let me go away now, for we have a family sacrifice in the city, and he, my brother, commanded me, and now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me slip away now, and see my brothers. ' He, therefore, did not come to the king's table."

And Shaul's wrath was kindled against Yehonatan, and he said to him, "You son of a straying woman deserving of punishment! Did I not know that you choose the son of Yishai, to your shame and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?
For all the days that the son of Yishai is living on the earth, you and your kingdom will not be established. And now, send and take him to me, for he is condemned to death."
And Yehonatan answered Shaul his father, and said to him, "Why should he be put to death? What has he done?"
And Shaul cast the spear upon him to strike him; and Yehonatan knew that it had been decided upon by his father, to put Dovid to death.
And Yehonatan arose from the table in fierce anger; and he did not eat any food on the second day of the new moon, for he was grieved concerning Dovid, for his father had put him to shame.
And it was in the morning, that Yehonatan went out at Dovid's appointed time, and a small boy was with him.
And he said to his boy, "Run, find now the arrows which I shoot." The boy ran; and he shot the arrow to cause it to go beyond him.
And the lad came up to the place of the arrow, which Yehonatan had shot. And Yehonatan called after the lad, and said, "Isn't the arrow beyond you?"
And Yehonatan called after the lad, "Quickly, hasten, do not stand!" And Yehonatan's lad gathered up the arrows, and came to his master.
And the lad knew nothing; only Yehonatan and Dovid knew the matter.
And Yehonatan gave his weapons to his boy, and said to him, "Go, bring to the city."

The lad departed, and Dovid arose from toward the south; and he fell upon his face to the ground three times, and prostrated himself three times. And they kissed one another, and wept one with the other, until Dovid exceeded.

And Yehonatan said to Dovid, "Go in peace! that we have sworn both of us in the name of Havayah, saying, 'May Havayah be between me and you, and between my descendants and your descendants forever.' "
And he arose and went away; and Yehonatan came to the city.
And Dovid came to Nov, to Achimelech the priest, and Achimelech came trembling toward Dovid, and said, "Why are you alone, and no one with you?"

And Dovid said to Achimelech the priest, "The king charged me with a matter, and said to me, 'Let no man know anything concerning the matter upon which I am sending you, and with which I have charged you.' And I troubled the young men to a hidden, secret place.
And now, what is there in your possession? Five loaves of bread? Give them into my hand, or whatever is found."
And the priest answered Dovid, and said, "There is no ordinary bread in my possession, but there is holy bread, if the young men have but kept themselves from women."

And Dovid answered the priest, and said to him, "But, women are withheld from us as of yesterday and the day before yesterday when I left, and the young men's garments are hallowed, and that is in a manner common, and even if today it would be hallowed in the vessel."
And the priest gave him hallowed, for there was no bread there, except the showbread, which was removed from before Havayah, to place warm bread on the day it was taken.
And there was a man of Shaul's servants on that day, detained before Havayah: and his name was Doeg the Edomi, the chief of Shaul's shepherds.
And Dovid said to Achimelech, "And if there is here in your possession a spear or a sword, for neither my sword nor my weapons have I taken in my hand, for the king's business was urgent."

And the priest said, "The sword of Golyat the Pelishti, whom you slew in the valley of the terebinth, behold, it is wrapped in a garment behind the ephod. If you wish to take that for yourself, take it, for there is none besides it here." And Dovid said, "There is none like it; give it to me."
And Dovid arose, and fled on that day from before Shaul; and he came to Achish the king of Gat.

And the bondsmen of Achish said to him, "Is this not Dovid, the king of the land? Was it not of this one that they would sing out with musical instruments, saying, 'Shaul has slain his thousands, and Dovid his ten thousands?' "
And Dovid took these words to heart, and became very much afraid of Achish the king of Gat.
And he changed his speech before their eyes, and he feigned insanity before them. And he scribbled on the doors of the gate, and let his saliva run down upon his beard.
And Achish said to his bondsmen, "Behold, you see a man who is mad. Why do you bring him to me?
Do I lack lunatics, that you have brought this one to rave in my presence? Will this one come into my house?"
And Dovid went away from there, and escaped to the cave of Adulam. And his brothers and all his father's household heard, and went down to him there.

And every man who was in distress, and every man who had a creditor, and every man of embittered spirit, gathered themselves to him, and he became a chief over them; and there were about four hundred men with him.
And Dovid went from there to Mitzpeh Moav, and he said to the king of Moav, "Let my father and mother come out now with you, until I know what Elokim will do for me."
And he brought them before the king of Moav; and they stayed with him all the time that Dovid was in the stronghold.
And Gad the prophet said to Dovid, "You shall not stay in the stronghold. Go and enter the land of Yehudah." And Dovid went, and came to the forest of Cheret.

And Shaul heard that Dovid and the men who were with him had become known, and Shaul was sitting in Givah under the tamarisk tree on a hill, and his spear was in his hand, and all his servants were standing by him.

And Shaul said to his servants who were standing by him, "Hearken now, O Binyaminim, will the son of Yishai also give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he appoint all of you captains of thousands and captains of hundreds?

For all of you have rebelled against me, and no one reveals to me when my son made a covenant with the son of Yishai, and no one of you feels sorry for me, or reveals to me that my son has incited my servant to rise up against me, to lie in wait as of this day."
Then Doeg the Edomi, who was appointed over Shaul's servants, answered and said, "I saw the son of Yishai come to Nov, to Achimelech the son of Achituv.
And he inquired of Havayah on his behalf, and gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Golyat the Pelishti."
And the king sent to call Achimelech the son of Achituv, the priest, and all of his father's household, the priests who were in Nov; and they all came to the king.
And Shaul said, "Listen now, O son of Achituv." And he said, "Here I am, my master."

And Shaul said to him, "Why have you rebelled against me, you and the son of Yishai, by your giving him food and a sword, and by inquiring of Elokim on his behalf, to rise up against me as one who lies in wait as of this day?"
And Achimelech answered the king, and said, "Now, who among all your servants is as faithful as Dovid, who is the king's son-in-law, and who goes to do your service, and is honored in your house?

Have I begun today to inquire of Elokim on his behalf? Far be it from me. Let not the king impute anything to his servant nor to all my father's household, for your servant knew nothing of all this, less, or more."
And the king said, "You shall surely die, Achimelech, you and all your father's household."

And the king said to the footmen who were standing beside him, "Turn and put the priests of Havayah to death, for their hand is also with Dovid, and because they knew that he was fleeing, and they did not inform me." And the king's servants would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of Havayah.
And the king said to Doeg, "You turn, and fall upon the priests." And Doeg turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day eighty-five men, wearers of the linen ephod.
And Nov, the city of the priests, he smote with the sharp edge of the sword, both man and woman, infant and suckling, and ox and ass, and lamb, with the sharp edge of the sword.
And one son of Achimelech the son of Achituv, whose name was Evyatar, escaped and fled after Dovid.
And Evyatar told Dovid that Shaul had slain the priests of Havayah.
And Dovid said to Evyatar, "I knew on that day that Doeg the Edomi was there, that he would tell Shaul. I brought about the death of every person of your father's household!
Stay with me; fear not, for he who seeks my soul seeks your soul, for you shall be in safeguard with me."
And they told Dovid, saying, "Behold, the Pelishtim are waging war against Ke'ilah, and they are pillaging the threshing- floors."
And Dovid inquired of Havayah, saying, "Shall I go and smite these Pelishtim?" And Havayah said to Dovid, "Go, and you shall smite the Pelishtim, and save Ke'ilah."
And Dovid's men said to him, "Behold, we are afraid here in Yehudah; how much more if we go to Ke'ilah, to the battle array of the Pelishtim?"
And Dovid continued further to inquire of Havayah, and Havayah answered him and said, "Arise, go down to Ke'ilah, for I am giving the Pelishtim into your hand."
And Dovid and his men went to Ke'ilah, and battled the Pelishtim, and he led away their cattle, and struck them a great blow, and Dovid saved the inhabitants of Ke'ilah.
And it was that when Evyatar the son of Achimelech fled to Dovid, to Ke'ilah, the ephod came down in his hand.
And it was related to Shaul that Dovid had come to Ke'ilah, and Shaul said, "Elokim has delivered him into my hand, for he has been shut in by coming into a city with doors and bars."
And Shaul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Ke'ilah, to besiege Dovid and his men.
And Dovid knew that upon him, Shaul was plotting the evil; and he said to Evyatar the priest, "Bring near the ephod."
And Dovid said, "O Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, Your bondsman has heard that Shaul seeks to come to Ke'ilah to destroy the city because of me.
Will the citizens of Ke'ilah deliver me into his hand? Will Shaul come down, as Your bondsman has heard? O Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, tell now Your bondsman!" And Havayah said, "He will come down."
And Dovid said, "Will the citizens of Ke'ilah deliver me and my men into Shaul's hands?" And Havayah said, "They will deliver."

And Dovid and his men, about six hundred men, arose and left Ke'ilah, and they went wherever they would go, and it was told to Shaul that Dovid had escaped from Ke'ilah, and he refrained from going forth.
And Dovid dwelt in the desert, in the strongholds, and he dwelt in the mountain in the Desert of Zif, and Shaul sought him all the days, but Elokim did not deliver him into his hand.
And Dovid saw that Shaul had gone forth to seek his soul, and Dovid was in the Desert of Zif, in the forest.
And Yehonatan, Shaul's son, arose and went to Dovid to the forest, and he strengthened his hand through Elokim.
And he said to him, "Fear not, for the hand of my father Shaul will not find you, and you shall reign over Yisroel, and may I be to you as a viceroy, and my father Shaul too, knows so."
And the two of them made a covenant before Havayah; and Dovid stayed in the forest, and Yehonatan went to his home.
And the Zifim went up to Shaul, to Givah, saying, "Is Dovid not hiding with us in the strongholds, in the forest, in the hill of Hachilah, which is from the south of the Desolate Wasteland?
And now, according to all the desires of your heart to come down, come down, and it is incumbent upon us to deliver him into the king's hand."
And Shaul said, "Blessed shall you be to Havayah, for you have taken pity upon me.
Go now, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his foot will be. Who saw him there? For told me that he deals cunningly.

And see and know of all the hiding places where he hides, and you shall return to me with the certainty, and I shall go with you, and it shall be that if he is in the land, I shall search him out among the thousands of Yehudah."
And they arose and went to Zif before Shaul, and Dovid and his men were in the Desert of Ma'on, in the plain which is to the south of the Desolate Wasteland.
And Shaul and his men went to search, and they told Dovid, and he went down to the rock, and stayed in the Desert of Ma'on, and Shaul heard and pursued Dovid in the Desert of Ma'on.

And Shaul went from this side of the mountain, and Dovid and his men were on that side of the mountain; and Dovid was hastening to get away from before Shaul, but Shaul and his men were encircling to Dovid and his men, to seize them.
And a messenger came to Shaul, saying, "Make haste and go, for the Pelishtim have spread out over the land!"
And Shaul returned from pursuing Dovid, and he went toward the Pelishtim. Therefore, they called that place the Rock of the Divisions.
And Dovid went up from there, and he stayed in the strongholds of Ein-Gedi.
And it was, when Shaul had returned from following the Pelishtim, that they told him, saying, "Dovid is in the Desert of Ein-Gedi."
And Shaul took three thousand picked men from all Yisroel, and went to seek Dovid and his men on the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
And he came to the sheepcotes on the way, and there was a cave, and Shaul went in to cover his feet, while Dovid and his men were staying at the end of the cave.

And Dovid's men said to him, "Behold the day concerning which Havayah said to you, 'Behold, I shall deliver your enemy into your hand; and you shall do to him as it will seem good in your eyes.' " And Dovid arose, and secretly severed the skirt of Shaul's coat.
And it was afterwards, that Dovid's heart smote him, for he had severed Shaul's skirt.
And he said to his men, "Havayah forbid it for me, that I should do this thing to my master, to Havayah's anointed, to stretch forth my hand upon him, for he is Havayah's anointed."
And Dovid stayed his men with these words, and did not allow them to rise up against Shaul, and Shaul arose from the cave and went on the way.
And Dovid arose afterwards and emerged from the cave after Shaul, saying, "My master the King!" And Shaul looked behind him, and Dovid bowed with his face to the ground, and prostrated himself.
And Dovid said to Shaul, "Why should you listen to the words of a man, saying, 'Behold, Dovid seeks your harm'?

Behold, this day your eyes have seen how Havayah delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and said to kill you, but had pity on you, and I said, 'I shall not stretch forth my hand against my master, for he is Havayah's anointed.'

And Father, see! Also, see the skirt of your coat in my hand, for in that I severed the skirt of your coat and I did not kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, but you are stalking my soul to take it.
May Havayah judge between me and you, and may Havayah avenge me of you, but my hand shall not be upon you.
As says the proverb of the ancient one; 'From the wicked comes forth wickedness,' and my hand shall not be upon you.
After whom has the king of Yisroel come forth? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A single flea?
And Havayah shall become a judge, and He shall judge between me and you, and He shall see and plead my cause, and exact justice for me from your hand."
And it was, when Dovid finished speaking these words to Shaul, that Shaul said, "Is this your voice, my son Dovid?" And Shaul raised his voice and wept.
And he said to Dovid, "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with goodness, while I have repaid you with evil.
And you have shown today how you have dealt well with me, how Havayah delivered me into your hand, and you did not kill me.
For when a man finds his enemy, does he send him away safely? And may Havayah repay you with goodness for what you have done to me on this day.
And now, behold, I know that you will reign, and the kingdom of Yisroel will be established in your hand.
And now, swear to me by Havayah, that you will not cut off my seed, and you will not destroy my name from my father's house."
And Dovid swore to Shaul; and Shaul went to his home, and Dovid and his men went up to the stronghold.
And Shmuel died, and all Yisroel gathered, and lamented him, and they buried him in his house in Ramah. And Dovid arose, and went down to the Desert of Paran.
And there was a man in Ma'on, whose possessions were in Karmel. And the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats; and he was, while shearing his sheep, in Karmel.
And the man's name was Naval, and his wife's name was Avigayil. And the woman was of good sense and of beautiful form, but the man was hard, and of evil deeds; and he was a Kalevi.
And Dovid heard in the desert, that Naval was shearing his sheep.
And Dovid sent ten youths, and Dovid said to the youths, "Go up to Karmel, and you shall come to Naval, and greet him in my name.
And you shall say, 'So shall you be living next year, and may peace be to you, and peace to your household, and peace to all that is yours.
And now, I have heard that they are shearing for you. Now, your shepherds were with us. We did not disgrace them, neither was anything missing to them all the time they were in Karmel.
Ask your youths and they will tell you, and may the youths find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a festive day. Give now, what your hand will find, for your servants and for your son Dovid.' "
And Dovid's youths came, and spoke to Naval according to all these words, in Dovid's name, and they rested.
And Naval answered Dovid's servants, and said, "Who is Dovid, and who is the son of Yishai? Nowadays, there are many slaves, who break away, each one from his master.
Now, shall I take my bread and my water, and my meal which I have cooked for my shearers, and shall I give them to people of whom I know not whence they are?"
And Dovid's youths turned around to their way, and returned, and came and told him according to all these words.

And Dovid said to his men, "Gird each man his sword," and they girded each man his sword, and Dovid too, girded his sword, and they went up after Dovid, about four hundred men, and two hundred stayed with the luggage.
And one youth of the youths, told Avigayil, the wife of Naval, saying, "Behold, Dovid sent messengers from the desert to greet our master, and he drove them away.
And the men are very good to us; and we were not disgraced, nor was anything missing to us all the time we went with them, when we were in the field.
They were a wall over us both night and day, all the time we were with them, pasturing the sheep.
And now, know and see what you will do, for the evil has been decided upon against our master and against all of his household; and he is such a base person that one cannot speak to him."

And Avigayil hastened and she took two hundred loaves, and two earthenware jugs of wine, and five prepared sheep, and five seah of flour of roasted ears of grain, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs; and she placed them on the donkeys.
And she said to her youths, "Go on ahead of me. Behold, I am coming after you." And she did not tell her husband Naval.
And it was, that she was riding on the donkey, and coming down, under cover of the mountain, and behold, Dovid and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.
And Dovid said, "Surely in vain have I watched all this fellow has in the desert, so that nothing was missing of all that is his, and he has returned me evil for good.
So shall Elokim do to Dovid's enemies, and so shall He continue, if I leave over of all that he has, by the morning light, even one dog."
And Avigayil saw Dovid, and she hastened and leaned off the donkey; and she fell on her face before Dovid, and prostrated herself on the ground.
And she fell at his feet, and said, "In me alone, my master, is the iniquity. Now, let your handmaid speak into your ears, and hearken to the words of your handmaid.

Let not my master take heed of this base fellow, of Naval, for like his name, so is he. Naval is his name, and ungratefulness is with him: and I, your handmaid, did not see my master's youths whom you sent.

And now, my master, as Havayah lives and by your life, that Havayah has withheld you from coming to bloodshed, and from saving yourself with your hand. And now, may your enemies and those who seek evil to my master, be as Naval.
And now, this gift which your handmaid has brought to my master, shall be given to the youths who walk at my master's feet.
Forgive now your handmaid's transgression, for Havayah shall make for my master a sure house, for my master fights the wars of Havayah. And let no evil be found in you all your days.

And a man has arisen to pursue you and to seek your soul. But my master's soul shall be bound in the bundle of life with Havayah your Elokim, while the soul of your enemies, Havayah will sling it with the hollow of the sling.
And it will be, when Havayah will do to my master according to all the good which He spoke concerning you, and He will appoint you as ruler over Yisroel.

Let this not be to you as a stumbling block and a remorse of heart to my master, that you have shed blood without cause, or that my master has avenged himself. And when Havayah will do good to my master, you shall remember your maidservant."
And Dovid said to Avigayil, "Blessed is Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, Who has sent you towards me on this day.
Blessed is your advice, and blessed be you, who have restrained me this day from coming into bloodshed, and from avenging myself with my own hand.

And indeed, as Havayah Elokim of Yisroel lives, Who has restrained me from harming you, that had you not hastened and come toward me, there would not have been left to Naval until daybreak, even one dog."
And Dovid took from her hand that which she had brought him, and he said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See that I have hearkened to your voice and have shown you favor."

And Avigayil came to Naval, and behold, he had a feast in his house like the feast of the king; and Naval's heart was merry within him, and he was very drunk. And she did not tell him anything, less or more until daybreak.
And it was in the morning, when the wine had left Naval, that his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became like stone.
And it was just ten days after, that Havayah inflicted a stroke on Naval, and he died.

And Dovid heard that Naval had died, and he said, "Blessed is Havayah, Who has judged the cause of my reproach from the hand of Naval, and restrained His bondsman from evil, and returned Naval's evil upon his own head." And Dovid sent, and spoke concerning Avigayil to take her to him for a wife.
And Dovid's servants came to Avigayil, to Karmel, and spoke to her, saying, "Dovid has sent us to you to take you to him for a wife."
And she arose, and prostrated herself upon her face to the ground, and said, "Behold, your bondswoman is a slave to wash the feet of my master's servants."
And she hastened, and mounted the donkey with her five maidens who went with her. And she went after Dovid's messengers, and became his wife.
And Dovid took Achinoam from Yizre'el, and they both became his wives.
And Shaul had given his daughter, Michal, wife of Dovid, to Palti the son of Layish, who was from Gallim.
And the Zifim came to Shaul, to Givah, saying, "Is not Dovid hiding in the Hill of Hachilah, before the Desolate Wasteland?"
And Shaul arose and descended to the Desert of Zif, and with him were three thousand picked men, to seek Dovid in the Desert of Zif.

And Shaul encamped in the Hill of Hachilah, which is before the Desolate Wasteland, by the road. And Dovid was staying in the desert; and it appeared to him that Shaul had come after him to the desert.
And Dovid sent spies, and he learned that Shaul had surely come.

And Dovid arose and came to the place where Shaul had encamped. And Dovid saw the place where Shaul lay, and Avner the son of Ner, the commander of his army. And Shaul was lying within the barricade, and the people were encamped around him.

And Dovid spoke up and said to Achimelech the Chitti and to Avishai the son of Tzeruyah, the brother of Yoav, saying, "Who will go down with me to Shaul to the camp?" And Avishai said, "I shall go down with you."

And Dovid and Avishai came to the people by night, and behold, Shaul was lying asleep within the barricade with his spear thrust into the ground at his head, and Avner and the people were lying around him.
And Avishai said to Dovid, "Today, Elokim has delivered your enemy into your hand; and now, let me strike him now, with the spear to the ground with one stroke; and I shall not repeat this to him."
And Dovid said to Avishai, "Do not destroy him, for who can stretch forth his hand against Havayah's anointed and be accounted guiltless?"
And Dovid said, "As Havayah lives, but Havayah will smite him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down to war and perish.
Far be it for me from Havayah to stretch forth my hand against Havayah's anointed. And now, take now the spear which is at his head and the jug of water, and let us go away."

And Dovid took the spear and the jug of water from near Shaul's head, and they went away. And no one saw and no one knew and no one awakened, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from Havayah had fallen upon them.
And Dovid crossed to the other side, and stood on the mountain peak from afar; the space between them was great.
And Dovid called the people and to Avner the son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Avner?" And Avner answered and said, "Who are you who have called the king?"
And Dovid said to Avner, "Are you not a valiant man? And who is like you in Yisroel? And why did you not guard your master the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king, your master.

This thing which you have done, is not good; as Havayah lives, you are worthy of death, for you did not keep watch over your master, over Havayah's anointed. And now, see where the king's spear is, and the jug of water which was at his head."
And Shaul recognized Dovid's voice, and said, "Is this your voice, my son Dovid," And Dovid said, " my voice, my master, O king."
And he said, "Why does my master pursue his servant? For what have I done? And what evil is in my hand?

And now, let now my master the king hear his servant's words. If Havayah has incited you against me, He will accept an offering; but if the sons of men, cursed be they before Havayah, for they have driven me today from cleaving to Havayah's heritage, saying, 'Go, worship other deities.'
And now, let not my blood fall to the ground away from the face of Havayah, for the king of Yisroel has gone out to seek a flea as the partridge hunts in the mountains."
And Shaul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son Dovid, for I shall harm you no more, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly and have erred exceedingly."
And Dovid answered and said, "Behold the king's spear. Now let one of the youths come over and take it.
And Havayah will repay every man for his righteousness and his faithfulness, for Havayah delivered you today into my hand, and I would not stretch forth my hand against Havayah's anointed.
And behold, as your life was precious this day in my eyes, so shall my life be precious in the eyes of Havayah, and He shall save me from every distress."
And Shaul said to Dovid, "Blessed be you, my son Dovid. You shall both do and you shall prevail." And Dovid went on his way, and Shaul returned to his place.

And Dovid said to himself, "Now, I shall perish one day in the hand of Shaul; there is nothing better for me than that I shall escape to the land of the Pelishtim, and Shaul will despair of me, to seek me any more in all the border of Yisroel, and I shall escape from his hand. "
And Dovid arose. And he and the six hundred men who were with him, crossed over to Achish the son of Maoch, the king of Gat.
And Dovid dwelt with Achish in Gat, he and his men, each man and his household, Dovid and his two wives; Achinoam the Yizre'elit and Avigayil the wife of Naval, the Karmelit.
And it was told to Shaul that Dovid had fled to Gat, and he did not continue to search for him.

And Dovid said to Achish, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the country towns, and I shall dwell there, for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?"
And Achish gave him Tziklag on that day; therefore, Tziklag has belonged to the kings of Yehudah until this day.
And the number of days which Dovid dwelt in the field of the Pelishtim was days and four months.
And Dovid and his men would go up and raid the Geshurim and the Gizrim and the Amalekim, for those were the inhabitants of the land, who were of old, as you go to Shur, even to the land of Mitzrayim.
And Dovid would smite the land, and leave neither man nor woman alive; and he would take sheep and cattle, and donkeys and camels and clothing, and return and come to Achish.
And Achish would say, "Where did you raid today?" And Dovid would say, "Against the south of Yehudah, and against the south of the Yerachme'elim and against the south of the Keinim."

And Dovid would leave alive neither man nor woman to bring to Gat, saying, "Lest they tell about us, saying, 'So has Dovid done, and so is his manner all the days which he has dwelt in the field of the Pelishtim.' "
And Achish believed Dovid, saying, "He has greatly abhorred his people Yisroel, and he will be to me a bondsman forever."

And it was in those days that the Pelishtim gathered their camps together for warfare, to make a war upon Yisroel. And Achish said to Dovid, "You shall know that you shall go out with me in the camp, you and your men."
And Dovid said to Achish, "Therefore, you shall know what your servant will do." And Achish said to Dovid, "Therefore, I shall make you my bodyguard all the time."
Now Shmuel had died, and all Yisroel lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, and in his own city. Now, Shaul had abolished necromancers and those who divine with the Yidoa bone from the land.
And the Pelishtim gathered, and came and encamped in Shunem. And Shaul gathered all Yisroel, and they encamped in Gilboa.
And Shaul saw the camp of the Pelishtim. And he feared, and his heart trembled greatly.
And Shaul inquired of Havayah, and Havayah did not answer; neither by dreams, nor by the Urim, nor by the prophets.
And Shaul said to his servants, "Seek for me a necromanceress; and I shall go to her, and inquire of her." And his servants said, "Behold, there is a necromanceress in Ein-Dor."

And Shaul disguised himself, and donned other garments. And he went, he and two men with him. And they came to the woman by night, and he said, "Divine now for me with necromancy, and conjure up for me whom I shall tell you."

And the woman said to him, "Behold, you know what Shaul has done, that he has abolished the necromancers and those who divine by the Yidoa bone, from the land; and why do you lay a snare for my life to cause me to die?"
And Shaul swore to her by Havayah, saying, "As Havayah lives, no punishment will happen to you for this thing."
And the woman said, "Whom shall I conjure up for you?" And he said, "Conjure up Shmuel for me."
And the woman saw Shmuel, and she cried aloud. And the woman said to Shaul, saying, "Why have you deceived me? For you are Shaul!"
And the king said to her, "Fear not, for what have you seen?" And the woman said to Shaul, "I have seen angels ascending from the earth."

And he said to her, "What is his form?" And she said, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a cloak." And Shaul knew that he was Shmuel; and he bowed down with his face to the ground, and prostrated himself.

And Shmuel said to Shaul, "Why have you roused me, to bring me up?" And Shaul said, "I am greatly distressed, and the Pelishtim are battling against me, and Elokim has turned away from me, and has not answered me anymore, neither through the prophets, nor through dreams. And I have called you to let me know what I shall do."
And Shmuel said, "And why do you ask me, when Havayah has turned away from you, and has become your adversary?
And Havayah has done to him as He spoke by me; and Havayah has torn the kingdom from your hand, and has given it to your fellow-to Dovid.
Because you did not listen to Havayah's voice, and you did not execute the fierceness of His wrath against Amalek; therefore, Havayah has done this thing to you this day.

And Havayah will also deliver Yisroel with you into the hand of the Pelishtim; and tomorrow, you and your sons will be with me. Also, Havayah will deliver the camp of Yisroel into the hand of the Pelishtim."

And Shaul hastened and fell his full length to the ground; and he was very frightened because of Shmuel's words. Furthermore, he had no strength, for he had not eaten bread all that day and all that night.

And the woman came to Shaul, and saw that he was very much terror-stricken. And she said to him, "Behold, your handmaid listened to your voice; and I have put my life in my hand, and obeyed your words which you spoke to me.
And now, I pray you, you also listen to the voice of your handmaid, and let me place before you a morsel of bread and eat; and you will have strength when you go on the way."
And he refused, and said, "I shall not eat." And his servants and also the woman urged him: and he listened to their voice. And he arose from the ground and sat upon the couch.
And the woman had a fatted calf in the house; and she hastened and slaughtered it. And she took flour and kneaded it and baked from it unleavened cakes.
And she set it before Shaul and before his servants, and they ate. And they rose and went away on that night.
And the Pelishtim gathered all their camps to Afek, and the Bnei Yisroel were encamped by the fountain which is in Yizre'el.
And the lords of the Pelishtim were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and Dovid and his men were passing in the rear with Achish.

And the officers of the Pelishtim said, "What are these Ivrim?" And Achish said to the officers of the Pelishtim, "Is this not Dovid, the servant of Shaul the king of Yisroel, who has been with me these days or these years, and I have found no fault in him from the day he fell until this day."

But the officers of the Pelishtim were enraged against him, and the officers of the Pelishtim said to him, "Return the man, and let him return to his place, where you have appointed him, and let him not go down with us into the battle, lest he become an adversary to us in the battle. And with what will this one reconcile himself to his master? Is it not with the heads of those men?
Is this not Dovid of whom they sang with musical instruments, saying, 'Shaul has slain his thousands and Dovid his ten thousands.' "

And Achish called Dovid and said to him, "As Havayah lives, that you are upright, and your going out and coming in with me in the camp, is good in my eyes, for I have not found in you any evil from the day of your coming to me until this day, but you are not good in the eyes of the lords.
And now, return and go peacefully, and do not do evil in the eyes of the lords of the Pelishtim."
And Dovid said to Achish, "But what have I done and what have you found in your bondsman until this day, that I shall not come and wage war against the enemies of my master the king?"
And Achish answered and said to Dovid, "I know that you are good in my eyes like an angel of Elokim, but the officers of the Pelishtim have said, 'Let him not go up with us into the battle.'
And now, arise early in the morning with your master's bondsmen who came with you, and you shall arise early in the morning when it is light for you, and go."
And Dovid arose early, he and his men to go in the morning to return to the land of the Pelishtim; and the Pelishtim went up to Yizre'el.
And it was, when Dovid and his men came to Tziklag, that on the third day, the Amalekim had raided the South and Tziklag, and they had smote Tziklag and burned it with fire.
And they had captured the women who were therein, but they slew no one, neither big nor small, but led them away and went on their way.
And Dovid and his men came to the city, and behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been captured.
And Dovid and all the people who were with him, raised their voice and wept, until they had no strength to weep.
And Dovid's two wives were captured: Achinoam the Yizre'elit and Avigayil the wife of Naval the Karmeli.

And Dovid was in dire straits, for the people spoke of stoning him, for the soul of all the people was grieved, each man concerning his sons and concerning his daughters; but Dovid strengthened himself in Havayah his Elokim.
And Dovid said to Evyatar the priest, the son of Achimelech, "Bring near to me now the ephod." And Evyatar brought the ephod near to Dovid.
And Dovid enquired of Havayah saying, "Shall I pursue this troop? Will I overtake them?" And He said to him, "Pursue, for you shall overtake and you shall rescue."
And Dovid went, he and six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Brook Besor, and those who were left behind stayed.
And Dovid pursued, he and four hundred men, and there remained two hundred men who refrained from crossing the Brook Besor.
And they found a Mitzri man in the field and brought him to Dovid. And they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his spirit returned to him: for he had eaten no bread nor drunk any water three days and three nights.
And Dovid said to him, "To whom do you belong, and from where are you?" And he said, "I am a Mitzri youth, a slave of an Amaleki man. And my master left me, for three days ago today I feel sick.
We made a raid upon the south of the Kereitim and upon that which belongs to Yehudah, and upon the south of Kalev; and we burned Tziklag with fire."

And Dovid said to him, "Will you bring me down to this troop?" And he said, "Swear to me by Elokim that you will not put me to death, and that you will not deliver me into my master's hand, and I shall bring you down to this troop."

And he brought him down, and behold, they were scattered over the entire landscape, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil which they had taken from the land of the Pelishtim and from the land of Yehudah.
And Dovid smote them from evening until evening to their morrow, and no man of them escaped except four hundred young men who rode on camels, and fled.
And Dovid rescued all that the Amalekim had taken, and Dovid rescued his two wives.
And there was nothing missing to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, nor anything which they had taken to themselves. Dovid recovered everything.
And Dovid took all the sheep and the cattle. They led before those cattle and said, "This is Dovid's spoil."

And Dovid came to the two hundred men who had refrained from going after Dovid and they had stationed them at the Brook Besor, and they came out toward Dovid and toward the people who were with him. And Dovid approached the people and greeted them.

Then every evil and unscrupulous man of the men who had gone with Dovid, spoke up, and said, "Since they did not go with me, let us not give them of the spoil which we have rescued, but each man his wife and his children, and let them lead them away and depart."
And Dovid said, "Do not do so, my brethren, with that which Havayah has given us, and He guarded us and delivered the troop which came upon us, into our hand.
And who will listen to you concerning this matter, for as the share of him who goes down into battle, so is the share of him who stays with the luggage; they shall share alike."
And it was from that day on, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Yisroel until this day.
And Dovid came to Tziklag and sent of the spoil to the elders of Yehudah, to his friends, saying, "Here is a present for you from the spoils of the enemies of Havayah."
To those who were in Beit El, and to those who were in Ramot of the South, and to those who were in Yattir.
And to those who were in Aro'er, and to those who were in Sifmot, and to those who were in Eshtemo'a.
And to those who were in Rachal, and to those who were in the cities of the Yerachme'elim, and to those who were in the cities of the Keinim.
And to those who were in Chormah, and to those who were in Kor-Ashan, and to those who were in Atach.
And to those who were in Chevron, and to all the places which Dovid and his men had frequented.
And the Pelishtim fought with Yisroel, and the men of Yisroel fled from before the Pelishtim, and the slain fell on Mt. Gilboa.
And the Pelishtim overtook Shaul and his sons, and the Pelishtim slew Yehonatan and Avinadav, and Malkishua, Shaul's sons.
And the battle fell heavy upon Shaul, and the archers found him, and he was very much frightened of the archers.

And Shaul said to his weapon-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and run me through and mock me." But his weapon-bearer was unwilling, for he was very much afraid. And Shaul took the sword and fell upon it.
And his weapon-bearer saw that Shaul had died, and he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
And Shaul and his three sons and his weapon-bearer died. Also, all his men died together on that day.

And the men of Yisroel who were on the other side of the valley, and who were on the other side of the Yarden, saw that the men of Yisroel had fled and that Shaul and his three sons had died; and they left the cities and fled, and the Pelishtim came and occupied them.
And it was on the morrow, that the Pelishtim came to strip the slain, and they found Shaul and his sons lying on Mt. Gilboa.
And they severed his head and stripped his armor; and they sent them around in the land of the Pelishtim, to spread the tidings to the house of their idols and to the people.
And they put his armor in the house of Ashtarot, and they impaled his body on the wall of Beit-She'an.
And the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gilad heard about him, that which the Pelishtim had done to Shaul.
And all the brave men rose and went all night and took Shaul's body and his sons' bodies from the wall of Beit-She'an, and they came to Yavesh and burned them there.
And they took their bones and buried them under the tree in Yavesh, and they fasted seven days.
